  89     channel_width_mhz: NDArray[np.floating]
  90     noise_std: NDArray[np.floating]
  91     sample_interval_s: float
  92     time0_unix_ns: int
  93     reference_frequency_mhz: float
  94     dispersion: DispersionState

  97     _gain_inverse_noise: NDArray[np.floating] = field(init=False, repr=False)
  98     _gain_data_quadratic: NDArray[np.floating] = field(init=False, repr=False)
  99     _gain_log_constant: NDArray[np.floating] = field(init=False, repr=False)
 100     _kernel_time_s: NDArray[np.floating] = field(init=False, repr=False)
 101     _kernel_frequency_mhz: NDArray[np.floating] = field(init=False, repr=False)
 102     _kernel_dispersion_basis_s: NDArray[np.floating] = field(init=False, repr=False)
 103 
 104     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
 105         self.waterfall = np.asarray(self.waterfall, dtype=float)
 106         self.valid = np.asarray(self.valid, dtype=bool)
 107         self.frequency_mhz = np.asarray(self.frequency_mhz, dtype=float)
 108         widths = np.asarray(self.channel_width_mhz, dtype=float)
 109         noise = np.asarray(self.noise_std, dtype=float)
 110         if self.instrument not in {"chime", "dsa"}:
 111             raise ValueError(f"unsupported instrument: {self.instrument!r}")
 112         if self.waterfall.ndim != 2:
 113             raise ValueError("waterfall must have shape (frequency, time)")
 114         if self.valid.shape != self.waterfall.shape:
 115             raise ValueError("valid mask must match the waterfall")
 116         nfreq = self.waterfall.shape[0]
 117         if self.frequency_mhz.shape != (nfreq,):
 118             raise ValueError("frequency_mhz must contain one center per row")
 119         if widths.ndim == 0:
 120             widths = np.full(nfreq, float(widths))
 121         if widths.shape != (nfreq,) or np.any(widths <= 0):
 122             raise ValueError("channel_width_mhz must be positive per row")
 123         if noise.ndim == 1:
 124             if noise.shape != (nfreq,):
 125                 raise ValueError("row noise must contain one value per row")
 126             noise = np.broadcast_to(noise[:, None], self.waterfall.shape).copy()
 127         if noise.shape != self.waterfall.shape:
 128             raise ValueError("noise_std must be per-row or per-pixel")
 129         if not np.isclose(
 130             self.reference_frequency_mhz,
 131             REFERENCE_FREQUENCY_MHZ,
 132             rtol=0.0,
 133             atol=0.0,
 134         ):
 135             raise ValueError("joint timing requires a 400 MHz reference")
 136         if self.sample_interval_s <= 0:
 137             raise ValueError("sample_interval_s must be positive")
 138         if np.any(~np.isfinite(self.frequency_mhz)) or np.any(self.frequency_mhz <= 0):
 139             raise ValueError("frequency centers must be finite and positive")
 140         if not np.any(self.valid):
 141             raise ValueError("observation has no valid pixels")
 142         if np.any(~np.isfinite(self.waterfall[self.valid])):
 143             raise ValueError("valid waterfall pixels must be finite")
 144         if np.any(~np.isfinite(noise[self.valid])) or np.any(noise[self.valid] <= 0):
 145             raise ValueError("valid pixels require finite positive noise")
 146         self.channel_width_mhz = widths
 147         self.noise_std = noise
 148         safe_noise = np.where(self.valid, noise, 1.0)
 149         self._gain_whitened_data = np.where(
 150             self.valid, self.waterfall / safe_noise, 0.0
 151         )
 152         self._gain_inverse_noise = np.where(self.valid, 1.0 / safe_noise, 0.0)
 153         self._gain_data_quadratic = np.einsum(
 154             "ft,ft->f", self._gain_whitened_data, self._gain_whitened_data
 155         )
 156         self._gain_log_constant = (
 157             -0.5 * self.valid.sum(axis=1) * math.log(2.0 * math.pi)
 158             - np.where(self.valid, np.log(safe_noise), 0.0).sum(axis=1)
 159         )
 160         self._kernel_time_s = np.arange(self.waterfall.shape[1], dtype=float) * float(
 161             self.sample_interval_s
 162         )
 163         self._kernel_frequency_mhz = (
 164             self.frequency_mhz[:, None]
 165             + 0.5 * self.channel_width_mhz[:, None] * _RESPONSE_NODE
 166         )
 167         self._kernel_dispersion_basis_s = K_DM_S_MHZ2 * (
 168             self._kernel_frequency_mhz**-2 - REFERENCE_FREQUENCY_MHZ**-2
 169         )
 170         # The gain and kernel terms above are precomputed from these arrays;
 171         # freeze them so later mutation cannot desynchronize the cached terms.
 172         for array in (
 173             self.waterfall,
 174             self.valid,
 175             self.frequency_mhz,
 176             self.channel_width_mhz,
 177             self.noise_std,
 178         ):
 179             array.setflags(write=False)
 180

 182     def time_s(self) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 183         return self._kernel_time_s

 619 def _prior_transform(unit: NDArray[np.floating], layout: _RunLayout) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 620     output = np.empty(len(layout.parameters), dtype=float)
 621     for index, (value, parameter) in enumerate(zip(unit, layout.parameters, strict=True)):
 622         clipped = float(np.clip(value, 1.0e-12, 1.0 - 1.0e-12))
 623         if parameter.kind == "uniform":
 624             output[index] = parameter.low + clipped * (parameter.high - parameter.low)
 625         elif parameter.kind == "log_uniform":
 626             output[index] = math.exp(
 627                 math.log(parameter.low)
 628                 + clipped * (math.log(parameter.high) - math.log(parameter.low))
 629             )
 630         else:
 631             output[index] = parameter.low + parameter.high * float(ndtri(clipped))
 632     return output

 642 def _component_kernels(
 643     request: JointFitRequest,
 644     observation: BandObservation,
 645     layout: _RunLayout,
 646     values: dict[str, float],
 647     morphology: Morphology,
 648 ) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 649     relative_time = (
 650         observation.time0_unix_ns - request.geometry.epoch_unix_ns
 651     ) * 1.0e-9 + observation._kernel_time_s
 652     evaluation_frequency = observation._kernel_frequency_mhz
 653     residual_dm = values["absolute_dm_pc_cm3"] - observation.dispersion.product_dm_pc_cm3
 654     dispersion_delay = residual_dm * observation._kernel_dispersion_basis_s
 655     timing_error = values[layout.timing_error_names[observation.instrument]]
 656     kernels = []
 657     ordered = sorted(
 658         (
 659             component
 660             for component in request.components
 661             if component.instrument == observation.instrument
 662         ),
 663         key=lambda component: component.center_sample,
 664     )
 665     for component in ordered:
 666         toa_name, width_name, index_name = layout.component_parameter_names[
 667             (component.instrument, component.component_id)
 668         ]
 669         matched = toa_name.startswith("toa_")
 670         if matched:
 671             center_400 = (
 672                 values[toa_name]
 673                 + request.geometry.site_delay_s[observation.instrument]
 674                 + timing_error
 675             )
 676         else:
 677             # This nuisance ToA is expressed in the same relative epoch but does
 678             # not use geometry and therefore cannot constrain the station delay.
 679             center_400 = values[toa_name]
 680         center = center_400 + dispersion_delay
 681         width = (
 682             values[width_name]
 683             * (evaluation_frequency / REFERENCE_FREQUENCY_MHZ) ** values[index_name]
 684         )
 685         if morphology == "scattering":
 686             tau = values["tau_1ghz_s"] * (evaluation_frequency / 1000.0) ** (
 687                 -values["scattering_alpha"]
 688             )
 689             evaluated = gaussian_exponential_density(
 690                 relative_time,
 691                 center.reshape(-1),
 692                 width.reshape(-1),
 693                 tau.reshape(-1),
 694             )
 695             evaluated = evaluated.reshape(
 696                 observation.waterfall.shape[0],
 697                 _RESPONSE_WEIGHT.size,
 698                 relative_time.size,
 699             )
 700             kernel = (
 701                 _RESPONSE_WEIGHT[0] * evaluated[:, 0]
 702                 + _RESPONSE_WEIGHT[1] * evaluated[:, 1]
 703                 + _RESPONSE_WEIGHT[2] * evaluated[:, 2]
 704             )
 705         else:
 706             kernel = np.zeros(
 707                 (observation.waterfall.shape[0], relative_time.size), dtype=float
 708             )
 709             for node_index, weight in enumerate(_RESPONSE_WEIGHT):
 710                 kernel += weight * gaussian_density(
 711                     relative_time,
 712                     center[:, node_index],
 713                     width[:, node_index],
 714                 )
 715         kernels.append(kernel)
 716     return np.asarray(kernels, dtype=float)

 719 def _gain_marginal_band(
 720     observation: BandObservation,
 721     kernels: NDArray[np.floating],
 722     gain_variance: float,
 723     *,
 724     return_model: bool = False,
 725 ) -> tuple[float, NDArray[np.floating] | None]:
 726     """Integrate channel/component gains under a fixed proper Gaussian prior."""
 727 
 728     ncomponent, nfrequency, _ = kernels.shape
 729     if ncomponent == 1:
 730         whitened_design = kernels[0] * observation._gain_inverse_noise
 731         gram = np.einsum("ft,ft->f", whitened_design, whitened_design)
 732         projection = np.einsum(
 733             "ft,ft->f", whitened_design, observation._gain_whitened_data
 734         )
 735         precision = gram + 1.0 / gain_variance
 736         if np.any(~np.isfinite(precision)) or np.any(precision <= 0):
 737             return -np.inf, None
 738         gains = projection / precision
 739         logdet = np.log1p(gain_variance * gram)
 740         if np.any(~np.isfinite(logdet)):
 741             return -np.inf, None
 742         quadratic = observation._gain_data_quadratic - projection * gains
 743         log_evidence = np.sum(
 744             -0.5 * quadratic - 0.5 * logdet + observation._gain_log_constant
 745         )
 746         if not return_model:
 747             return float(log_evidence), None
 748         model = np.full(observation.waterfall.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
 749         evaluated = kernels[0] * gains[:, None]
 750         model[observation.valid] = evaluated[observation.valid]
 751         return float(log_evidence), model
 752 
 753     log_evidence = 0.0
 754     model = np.full(observation.waterfall.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
 755     identity = np.eye(ncomponent)
 756     for row in range(nfrequency):
 757         use = observation.valid[row]
 758         if not np.any(use):
 759             continue
 760         data = observation.waterfall[row, use]
 761         noise = observation.noise_std[row, use]
 762         design = kernels[:, row, use].T
 763         whitened_data = data / noise
 764         whitened_design = design / noise[:, None]
 765         gram = whitened_design.T @ whitened_design
 766         projection = whitened_design.T @ whitened_data
 767         precision = gram + identity / gain_variance
 768         try:
 769             gains = np.linalg.solve(precision, projection)
 770         except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
 771             return -np.inf, None
 772         sign, logdet = np.linalg.slogdet(identity + gain_variance * gram)
 773         if sign <= 0:
 774             return -np.inf, None
 775         quadratic = float(whitened_data @ whitened_data - projection @ gains)
 776         log_evidence += (
 777             -0.5 * quadratic
 778             - 0.5 * float(logdet)
 779             - 0.5 * use.sum() * math.log(2.0 * math.pi)
 780             - float(np.log(noise).sum())
 781         )
 782         if return_model:
 783             model[row, use] = design @ gains
 784     return float(log_evidence), model if return_model else None

 808 def _weighted_quantiles(
 809     values: NDArray[np.floating],
 810     weights: NDArray[np.floating],

 880 def _structured_residual_correlation(
 881     observation: BandObservation,
 882     whitened_valid_residual: NDArray[np.floating],
 883 ) -> float:
 884     """Measure diagonal frequency-time structure without fitting it away."""
 885 
 886     frequency = observation.frequency_mhz
 887     time = np.arange(observation.waterfall.shape[1], dtype=float)
 888     frequency = (frequency - np.mean(frequency)) / np.std(frequency)
 889     time = (time - np.mean(time)) / np.std(time)
 890     selected = (frequency[:, None] * time[None, :])[observation.valid]
 891     residual = np.asarray(whitened_valid_residual, dtype=float)
 892     if np.std(residual) == 0 or np.std(selected) == 0:
 893         return 0.0
 894     return float(np.corrcoef(residual, selected)[0, 1])

1069     lower, median, upper = _weighted_quantiles(combined_values, combined_weights)
1070     return {
1071         "median": float(median),
1072         "lower": float(lower),
1073         "upper": float(upper),
1074         "error_minus": float(median - lower),
1075         "error_plus": float(upper - median),
1076     }
1077 
1078 
1079 def _mixture_derived_quantiles(
1080     runs: list[HypothesisFit],
1081     run_weights: NDArray[np.floating],
1082     parameter_names: tuple[str, ...],
1083     transform,
1084 ) -> dict[str, float]:
1085     values = []
1086     weights = []
1087     for run, run_weight in zip(runs, run_weights, strict=True):
1088         if any(name not in run.parameter_names for name in parameter_names):
1089             continue
1090         columns = [run.samples[:, run.parameter_names.index(name)] for name in parameter_names]
1091         values.append(np.asarray(transform(*columns), dtype=float))
1092         weights.append(run.sample_weights * float(run_weight))
1093     if not values:
1094         raise ValueError("derived posterior parameters are absent from every run")
1095     combined_values = np.concatenate(values)
1096     combined_weights = np.concatenate(weights)
1097     combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()
1098     lower, median, upper = _weighted_quantiles(combined_values, combined_weights)
1099     return {
1100         "median": float(median),
1101         "lower": float(lower),
1102         "upper": float(upper),
1103         "error_minus": float(median - lower),
1104         "error_plus": float(upper - median),
1105     }
1106 
1107 
1108 def _absolute_time_summary(relative: dict[str, float], epoch_unix_ns: int) -> dict[str, int]:
1109     return {
1110         "median": epoch_unix_ns + round(relative["median"] * 1.0e9),
1111         "lower": epoch_unix_ns + round(relative["lower"] * 1.0e9),
1112         "upper": epoch_unix_ns + round(relative["upper"] * 1.0e9),
1113         "error_minus_ns": round(relative["error_minus"] * 1.0e9),
1114         "error_plus_ns": round(relative["error_plus"] * 1.0e9),
1115     }
1116 
1117 
1118 def _dm_toa_covariance(
1119     runs: list[HypothesisFit],
1120     run_weights: NDArray[np.floating],
1121     toa_parameter: str,
1122 ) -> dict[str, float]:
1123     dm_values = []
1124     toa_values = []
1125     weights = []
1126     for run, run_weight in zip(runs, run_weights, strict=True):
1127         if toa_parameter not in run.parameter_names:
1128             continue
1129         dm_values.append(run.samples[:, run.parameter_names.index("absolute_dm_pc_cm3")])
1130         toa_values.append(run.samples[:, run.parameter_names.index(toa_parameter)])
1131         weights.append(run.sample_weights * float(run_weight))
1132     dm = np.concatenate(dm_values)
1133     toa = np.concatenate(toa_values)
1134     weight = np.concatenate(weights)
1135     weight /= weight.sum()
1136     dm_centered = dm - np.sum(weight * dm)
1137     toa_centered = toa - np.sum(weight * toa)
1138     covariance = float(np.sum(weight * dm_centered * toa_centered))
1139     dm_variance = float(np.sum(weight * dm_centered**2))
1140     toa_variance = float(np.sum(weight * toa_centered**2))
1141     denominator = math.sqrt(dm_variance * toa_variance)
1142     correlation = covariance / denominator if denominator > 0 else 0.0
1143     return {
1144         "covariance_pc_cm3_s": covariance,
1145         "correlation": float(correlation),
1146     }
1147 
1148 
1149 def _edge_status(summary: dict[str, float], bounds: tuple[float, float], fraction: float) -> bool:
1150     margin = fraction * (bounds[1] - bounds[0])
1151     return bool(summary["median"] <= bounds[0] + margin or summary["median"] >= bounds[1] - margin)
1152 
1153 
1154 def _mixture_edge_mass(
1155     runs: list[HypothesisFit],
1156     run_weights: NDArray[np.floating],
1157     parameter_name: str,
1158     bounds: tuple[float, float],
1159     fraction: float,
1160 ) -> float:
1161     lower = bounds[0] + fraction * (bounds[1] - bounds[0])
1162     upper = bounds[1] - fraction * (bounds[1] - bounds[0])
1163     mass = 0.0
1164     for run, run_weight in zip(runs, run_weights, strict=True):
1165         index = run.parameter_names.index(parameter_name)
1166         at_edge = (run.samples[:, index] <= lower) | (run.samples[:, index] >= upper)
1167         mass += float(run_weight) * float(np.sum(run.sample_weights[at_edge]))
1168     return mass
1169 
1170 
1171 def _plausible_runs(
1172     runs: list[HypothesisFit],
1173     selected_index: int,
1174 ) -> tuple[list[HypothesisFit], NDArray[np.floating]]:
1175     """Return every hypothesis that remains numerically plausible.
1176 
1177     For each run, its optimistic evidence is ``logZ + error`` while every
1178     competitor uses ``logZ - error``. The run remains plausible when its
1179     resulting normalized evidence weight exceeds float64 resolution. The
1180     point-estimate winner is always retained. This is numerical, not a
1181     scientific posterior-mass threshold.
1182     """
1183 
1184     log_evidence = np.asarray([run.log_evidence for run in runs], dtype=float)
1185     errors = np.asarray([run.log_evidence_error for run in runs], dtype=float)
1186     if np.any(~np.isfinite(log_evidence)):
1187         raise ValueError("log evidences must be finite")
1188     if np.any(~np.isfinite(errors)) or np.any(errors < 0):
1189         raise ValueError("log evidence errors must be finite and nonnegative")
1190     upper_weights = np.empty(len(runs), dtype=float)
1191     for index in range(len(runs)):
1192         shifted = log_evidence - errors
1193         shifted[index] = log_evidence[index] + errors[index]
1194         relative = shifted - np.max(shifted)
1195         weights = np.exp(relative)
1196         upper_weights[index] = weights[index] / weights.sum()
1197     resolution = np.finfo(float).eps
1198     plausible = [
1199         run
1200         for index, run in enumerate(runs)
1201         if index == selected_index or upper_weights[index] > resolution
1202     ]
1203     return plausible, upper_weights
1204 
1205 
1206 def fit_joint_event(request: JointFitRequest) -> JointFitResult:
1207     """Fit every declared morphology/association and combine their evidence.
1208 
1209     No file I/O occurs here. Workflow adapters own product loading, provenance,
1210     checkpointing, and rendering.
1211     """
1212 
1213     runs = [
1214         _fit_one(request, hypothesis, morphology)
1215         for morphology in request.settings.morphologies
1216         for hypothesis in request.associations
1217     ]
1218     log_evidence = np.asarray([run.log_evidence for run in runs])
1219     relative = log_evidence - np.max(log_evidence)
1220     run_weights = np.exp(relative)
1221     run_weights /= run_weights.sum()
1222     dm = _mixture_quantiles(runs, run_weights, "absolute_dm_pc_cm3")
1223     latent_ids = sorted(
1224         {match.latent_id for hypothesis in request.associations for match in hypothesis.matches}
1225     )
1226     geocentric_toas = {}
1227     topocentric_toas = {}
1228     covariance = {}
1229     for latent_id in latent_ids:
1230         parameter = f"toa_{latent_id}_s"
1231         summary = _mixture_quantiles(runs, run_weights, parameter)
1232         geocentric_toas[latent_id] = _absolute_time_summary(summary, request.geometry.epoch_unix_ns)
1233         topocentric_toas[latent_id] = {}
1234         for instrument in ("chime", "dsa"):
1235             derived = _mixture_derived_quantiles(
1236                 runs,
1237                 run_weights,
1238                 (parameter, f"timing_error_{instrument}_s"),
1239                 lambda toa, error, instrument=instrument: (
1240                     toa + request.geometry.site_delay_s[instrument] + error
1241                 ),
1242             )
1243             topocentric_toas[latent_id][instrument] = _absolute_time_summary(
1244                 derived, request.geometry.epoch_unix_ns
1245             )
1246         covariance[latent_id] = _dm_toa_covariance(runs, run_weights, parameter)
1247     median_at_edge = _edge_status(
1248         dm,
1249         request.settings.dm_bounds_pc_cm3,
1250         request.settings.posterior_edge_fraction,
1251     )
1252     edge_mass = _mixture_edge_mass(
1253         runs,
1254         run_weights,
1255         "absolute_dm_pc_cm3",
1256         request.settings.dm_bounds_pc_cm3,
1257         request.settings.posterior_edge_fraction,
1258     )
1259     edge = median_at_edge or (edge_mass > request.settings.maximum_prior_edge_mass)
1260     diagnostics = {
1261         "posterior_dm_at_edge": edge,
1262         "posterior_dm_median_at_edge": median_at_edge,
1263         "posterior_dm_edge_mass": edge_mass,
1264         "run_weights": {
1265             f"{run.morphology}:{run.association}": float(weight)
1266             for run, weight in zip(runs, run_weights, strict=True)
1267         },
1268         "reference_frequency_mhz": REFERENCE_FREQUENCY_MHZ,
1269         "separate_native_grids": True,
1270         "independent_band_centroids_allowed": False,
1271         "dm_toa_covariance": covariance,
1272     }
1273     best_index = int(np.argmax(run_weights))
1274     best_run = runs[best_index]
1275     best_hypothesis = next(
1276         hypothesis for hypothesis in request.associations if hypothesis.name == best_run.association
1277     )
1278     best_layout = _layout(request, best_hypothesis, best_run.morphology)
1279     plausible_runs, plausible_upper_weights = _plausible_runs(
1280         runs,
1281         best_index,
1282     )
1283     maximum_residual_power = max(
1284         float(band["reduced_residual_power"])
1285         for run in plausible_runs
1286         for band in run.diagnostics["bands"].values()
1287     )
1288     maximum_structured_correlation = max(
1289         abs(float(band["structured_frequency_time_correlation"]))
1290         for run in plausible_runs
1291         for band in run.diagnostics["bands"].values()
1292     )
1293     model_adequate = (
1294         maximum_residual_power <= request.settings.maximum_reduced_residual_power
1295         and maximum_structured_correlation
1296         <= request.settings.maximum_structured_residual_correlation
1297     )
1298     prior_railed = sorted(
1299         {name for run in plausible_runs for name in run.diagnostics["prior_rail_parameters"]}
1300     )
1301     diagnostics.update(
1302         {
1303             "maximum_reduced_residual_power": maximum_residual_power,
1304             "maximum_structured_residual_correlation": (maximum_structured_correlation),
1305             "model_adequate": model_adequate,
1306             "prior_rail_parameters": prior_railed,
1307             "plausible_runs": [
1308                 f"{run.morphology}:{run.association}" for run in plausible_runs
1309             ],
1310             "plausible_run_upper_weights": {
1311                 f"{run.morphology}:{run.association}": float(weight)
1312                 for run, weight in zip(runs, plausible_upper_weights, strict=True)
1313             },
1314             "plausible_run_weight_resolution": float(np.finfo(float).eps),
1315             "fixed_valid_pixel_masks": True,
1316         }
1317     )
1318     if edge:
1319         status = "failed_dm_edge"
1320     elif prior_railed:
1321         status = "failed_prior_rail"
1322     elif not model_adequate:
1323         status = "failed_model_inadequate"
1324     else:
1325         status = "provisional_pending_owner_approval"
1326     return JointFitResult(
1327         runs=tuple(runs),
1328         run_weights=run_weights,
1329         dm_pc_cm3=dm,
1330         geocentric_toa_unix_ns=geocentric_toas,
1331         topocentric_toa_unix_ns=topocentric_toas,
1332         model_products=_representative_models(request, best_run, best_layout),
1333         status=status,

=== CAMPAIGN_REPORT ===
# β-coherent thin-screen campaign — pass 1 report

Locked 2026-07-06 · branch `campaign/beta-thin-screen-pass1` · plan
`docs/rse/specs/plan-beta-coherent-thin-screen-campaign.md` · decision record
ADR-0006 (β co-model), ADR-0004 (rail semantics); ADR-0007 (thin vs extended)
deliberately deferred behind this pass.

## What was run

**Supersession note (2026-07-07):** this pass-1 report originally recorded the
historical JohnDoeII C2D1 run. The jointmodel-pair multiplicity audit superseded
that choice, and the promoted beta-coherent product now uses JohnDoeII C2D2.

All 12 CHIME–DSA co-detections were re-fit with the β-native joint model
(thin-screen PBF family: power-law-tail members for β < 4, exponential member
at the β = 4 square-law limit). β sampled with bounds (3.0, 4.0); α = 2β/(β−2)
derived, never sampled. Per-burst component multiplicity follows the locked
suffix map (`grade_beta_campaign.SUFFIX`):

| suffix | bursts |
|---|---|
| `_sharedzeta` | freya, casey, chromatica, wilhelm, hamilton |
| `_C1D1` | mahi |
| `_C2D1` | oran, isha |
| `_C2D2` | whitney_fine; johndoeII promoted |
| `_C2D4_cwin` | zach promoted (bespoke morphology-audit refit) |
| `_C3D3` | phineas |

Every fit was verified against its own posterior-predictive check before
grading (`fleet_status.json`); freya additionally passed the regression gate
against its reference run (|Δβ_ref| = 0.038 < 0.05). Runs root:
`$FLITS_RUNS/data/joint` (fit JSONs + `*_joint_samples*.npz` posteriors);
citable fit JSONs are copied into `analysis/beta_campaign/fits/`.

## Census (grader output, `beta_campaign_verdicts.{json,md}`)

Rail rule (ADR-0004): railed = within 3σ of a β bound OR ≥30% posterior mass
within 0.05 of the bound, from the sampled posterior (not the summary).

| burst | β (−/+) | α | τ₁ᴳᴴᶻ [ms] | χ²ᵣ C/D | rail | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| freya | 3.722 (−0.015/+0.014) | 4.32 | 0.119 | 1.29/1.03 | **interior** | MARGINAL |
| phineas | 3.228 (−0.018/+0.021) | 5.26 | 0.469 | 1.06/1.24 | **interior** | MARGINAL |
| casey | 3.990 | (4.0 limit) | 0.0186 | 1.57/1.02 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| mahi | 3.785 (−0.155/+0.138) | (4.0 limit) | 0.219 | 1.04/0.90 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| oran | 3.987 | (4.0 limit) | 0.843 | 1.02/1.22 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| isha | 3.841 (−0.105/+0.085) | (4.0 limit) | 0.314 | 1.05/0.91 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| johndoeII | 3.936 | (4.0 limit) | 2.219 | 1.09/1.23 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| whitney_fine | 3.968 | (4.0 limit) | 1.182 | 1.09/1.42 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| wilhelm | 3.979 | (4.0 limit) | 0.269 | 1.57/6.73 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |

| zach | 3.990 | (4.0 limit) | 0.186 | 1.35/1.02 | railed-hi | MARGINAL |
| chromatica | 3.990 | — | — | 11.59/9.25 | railed-hi | **FAIL** |

Headline: **2 interior members (freya, phineas) are genuine power-law-tail
detections**; the interior β for phineas (3.23) implies α = 5.26 — the
steepest in the sample. **10 posteriors rail at β = 4**: exponential-consistent,
α = 4 quotable only as a geometry-conditioned limit, and each is an ADR-0007
re-open candidate (an extended-medium PBF may fit these without railing).
No burst railed low or came back unconstrained. All gates cap at MARGINAL
because L3 τ×Δν was "not evaluable (no dnu_d)" at gate time — the two-screen
table below closes that observation gap out-of-band. chromatica FAILs L2
outright (χ²ᵣ ≈ 11.6/9.3; the montage shows its model panel flat against
strongly structured data) and is excluded from all citable products.

## Citable roster re-lock (`citable_alpha_roster.json`)

- **Tier A (7, fully adjudicated):** freya, phineas (interior β + derived α);
  casey, mahi, oran, isha, johndoeII (railed-hi, α = 4 limits).
- **Tier B (3, provisional):** wilhelm, hamilton, zach — railed-hi; wilhelm/hamilton

- **Multiplicity exemplar:** whitney (C2D2 after local re-prep) — quoted as
  exemplar, not a roster row.
- **Excluded:** chromatica (gate FAIL).

## Two-screen consistency (`two_screen_consistency.{json,md}`, DSA band)

**SUPERSEDED / SCIENTIFICALLY INVALID.** This calculation paired free-alpha
joint-fit tau with DSA bandwidths. The accepted policy requires fixed-index
`tau_consistency` refits, so none of the former same-screen/different-screen
verdicts is current. Exact JSON/Markdown outputs are preserved under
`.archive/outdated-science/2026-07-17/analysis/beta_campaign/` for audit.

## Sightline budget integration (`results/sightline_dm_scattering_budget.*`)

Campaign τ posteriors flow into the budget through the roster's `fit_json`
overrides (`galaxies/foreground/tau_consistency.py`). Coverage semantics
(survey_coverage.csv, exact-MOC footprints): a burst outside a survey's
footprint is **unconstrained by that survey, never "no foreground"**; deep
constraint requires a deep survey (DESI DR8-N / SDSS DR12) row that is
footprint_empty or has foreground/with-z hits. Consequences visible in the
regenerated budget: oran and mahi read "intervening screen unconstrained
(not excluded)"; hamilton's predicted intervening τ plausibly dominates its
measurement (pred/obs = 0.68 — consistent with its same_screen verdict
above); chromatica carries no measured τ.

\subsubsection{Gain-marginalized likelihood}
\label{sec:gainmarg}
\label{sec:beta-gainmarg}

The per-channel amplitude of an FRB spectrum is unknown and strongly modulated
by scintillation; carried as a free spectral envelope it leaves correlated
structure in the fit residuals and invalidates a $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test.
We therefore marginalize the per-channel gain analytically. With a Gaussian
prior on the gain the per-channel evidence is available in closed form (a
matched-filter likelihood), and the recovered gain absorbs both the burst
spectrum and the scintillation pattern. This removes the spectral and
scintillation structure from the residual, so that the reduced $\chi^2$ and the
lag-1 residual autocorrelation become meaningful quality gates, and it lowers
the sampled dimensionality.

Because the marginalization deliberately absorbs the scintillation pattern into
the gain, the scattering fit does not measure scintillation. The
decorrelation-bandwidth products used later
(Section~\ref{sec:results-scintillation}) come from a separate
autocorrelation-function analysis path applied to the same dynamic spectra, not
from this likelihood. The one interaction to guard against is at low
signal-to-noise, where a fully free per-channel gain can absorb genuine
scattering-induced spectral smearing into the spectral envelope and thereby bias
the scattering time low; we therefore keep the gain prior informative (finite
width) rather than flat, and verify on the final fits that the
$\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ posterior is stable against the gain-prior width before
quoting any low-$\tau$ result. The gain prior is a per-channel zero-mean
Gaussian of variance $s^2$; unless stated otherwise $s^2$ is profiled at its
maximum-marginal-likelihood value, and it is held fixed whenever Bayesian
evidences are compared across likelihood variants
(Section~\ref{sec:multicomp}), so that evidence differences reflect the
temporal model rather than the gain hyperparameter.

The priors on the sampled parameters are deliberately simple and, except for
one anchor, independent of the initialization, as evidence-based model
comparison requires. $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ and each intrinsic width
$\zeta$ are log-uniform over $10^{-4}$--$10^{3}$\,ms. $\beta$ is uniform over
the thin-screen inertial branch, by default $3\le\beta\le4$, the image of
$4\le\alpha\le6$ under $\alpha=2\beta/(\beta-2)$. A prior uniform in $\beta$
is not uniform in $\alpha$: the induced prior density on $\alpha$ scales as
$(\beta-2)^{2}$ and is four times higher at the $\beta=4$ endpoint than at
$\beta=3$, mildly favoring the square-law limit. A posterior concentrating at
$\beta=4$ is therefore treated as endpoint-degenerate
(Section~\ref{sec:jointfit}), not as a prior-independent detection of
square-law statistics. Each per-band
$\delta\mathrm{DM}$ is uniform over $\pm50\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ about the
dedispersion reference; bounding the residual keeps a broad, heavily
smeared solution from escaping into an unphysically large
$|\delta\mathrm{DM}|$ degeneracy. Each arrival time $t_0$ is uniform in
a window anchored on that band's profile-peak estimate, the only
data-derived quantity in the prior.

We sample the posterior by nested
sampling \citep{Skilling2004}, as implemented in \texttt{dynesty}
\citep{Speagle2020}, using random-walk sampling with at least 600 live
points (at least 800 for the higher-dimensional multi-component variants)
and terminating when the estimated remaining log-evidence falls below 0.5.
Parameter summaries are posterior-weighted percentiles, and the $\alpha$
posterior is derived deterministically from the $\beta$ samples. Each fit is
quality-gated on two criteria: the reduced $\chi^2$ of its noise-whitened,
gain-marginalized residuals (accepted in $0.3\le\chi^2_\mathrm{red}\le1.5$,
rejected above 10, and flagged for individual inspection between---or
suspiciously below 0.3), and the absence of lag-one residual
autocorrelation (Durbin--Watson statistic within 1--3). $R^2$ and
residual normality are treated as informational.

\subsubsection{Multiple temporal components}
\label{sec:multicomp}
\label{sec:beta-multicomp}

   5 burst runs at its previously adjudicated multiplicity (ADR-0005 / grade_allexp

  27 from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

  29 REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]

  32 RUNS = Path(os.environ.get("FABER2026_RUNS", "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/scratch/flits-local-runs"))

  39 # burst, nlive, model flags, output suffix (must mirror the runner's tag logic)

  65 def run_one(burst: str, nlive: int, flags: list[str], suffix: str, nproc: int) -> dict:

   1 #!/usr/bin/env python
   2 """Sim-injection gate for the beta-coherent thin-screen campaign (Phase 3).
   3 
   4 Three synthetic two-band injections routed through the PRODUCTION joint path
   5 (fit_joint_scattering, shared-zeta gain-marginal, campaign-default beta prior),
   6 not a private likelihood, so the gate exercises exactly the code the fleet
   7 will run (plan: docs/rse/specs/plan-beta-coherent-thin-screen-campaign.md):
   8 
   9   interior-3.7  beta_true=3.70  -> recover within 3 sigma, un-railed
  10   interior-3.3  beta_true=3.30  -> recover within 3 sigma, un-railed
  11                 (heavier t^-1.65 tail; wider CHIME window so the tail shape,
  12                 not its truncation, drives beta -- run_beta_poc.py rationale)
  13   rail-4.0      beta_true=4.00  -> the forward model dispatches the analytic
  14                 exponential member; the posterior must RAIL at the beta=4
  15                 bound (ADR-0004: median within 3 sigma of the prior edge)
  16 
  17 Injection physics (grids, gains, noise) is reused from the freya POC
  18 (analysis/beta_poc/run_beta_poc.py) so truth construction stays single-source.
  19 
  20   conda run -n flits python analysis/beta_campaign/sim_gate.py [--nlive N]
  21 
  22 Exit 0 iff all three verdicts are correct; the fleet must not launch otherwise.
  23 """
  24 
  25 from __future__ import annotations
  26 
  27 import argparse
  28 import importlib.util
  29 import json
  30 import sys
  31 from pathlib import Path
  32 
  33 import numpy as np
  34 
  35 
  36 REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
  37 sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
  38 
  39 from scattering.scat_analysis.burstfit_init import data_driven_initial_guess  # noqa: E402
  40 from scattering.scat_analysis.burstfit_joint import fit_joint_scattering  # noqa: E402
  41 
  42 _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
  43     "run_beta_poc", REPO / "analysis" / "beta_poc" / "run_beta_poc.py"
  44 )
  45 _poc = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
  46 _spec.loader.exec_module(_poc)
  47 
  48 CASES = [
  49     # (name, beta_true, tau_1ghz_ms, chime_t_max_ms, expect_rail)
  50     ("interior-3.7", 3.70, 0.05, 32.0, False),
  51     ("interior-3.3", 3.30, 0.03, 48.0, False),
  52     ("rail-4.0", 4.00, 0.05, 32.0, True),
  53 ]
  54 BETA_BOUNDS = (3.0, 4.0)  # campaign default (alpha in [4, 6])
  55 
  56 
  57 def _make_bands(beta: float, tau: float, t_max_C: float, seed: int):
  58     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
  59     n_time_C = int(448 * t_max_C / 32.0)  # keep the POC's dt when widening the window
  60     m_C0 = _poc._build_band(_poc.CHIME, n_freq=48, t_max=t_max_C, n_time=n_time_C)
  61     m_D0 = _poc._build_band(_poc.DSA, n_freq=48, t_max=6.0, n_time=320)
  62     m_C = _poc._inject(m_C0, tau, beta, _poc.ZETA1_TRUE, _poc.X_ZETA_TRUE, _poc.T0_C_TRUE, rng)
  63     m_D = _poc._inject(m_D0, tau, beta, _poc.ZETA1_TRUE, _poc.X_ZETA_TRUE, _poc.T0_D_TRUE, rng)
  64     return m_C, m_D
  65 
  66 
  67 def _init_for(m):
  68     return data_driven_initial_guess(
  69         data=m.data, freq=m.freq, time=m.time, dm=0.0, verbose=False
  70     ).params
  71 
  72 
  73 def _railed(med: float, err_minus: float, err_plus: float) -> bool:
  74     lo, hi = BETA_BOUNDS
  75     return (med - 3.0 * err_minus <= lo) or (med + 3.0 * err_plus >= hi)
  76 
  77 
  78 def run_case(name, beta_true, tau, t_max_C, expect_rail, nlive, nproc, seed, maxcall):
  79     m_C, m_D = _make_bands(beta_true, tau, t_max_C, seed)
  80     res = fit_joint_scattering(
  81         model_C=m_C,
  82         init_C=_init_for(m_C),
  83         model_D=m_D,
  84         init_D=_init_for(m_D),
  85         beta_bounds=BETA_BOUNDS,
  86         nlive=nlive,
  87         nproc=nproc,
  88         shared_zeta=True,
  89         verbose=False,
  90         rstate=np.random.default_rng(seed + 1),
  91         # POC-proven budget (run_beta_poc.py defaults): bounds the gate's
  92         # wall-time; recovery at this scale was 0.3% on beta
  93         maxcall=maxcall,
  94     )
  95     b = res["percentiles"]["beta"]
  96     med, em, ep = b["median"], b["err_minus"], b["err_plus"]
  97     railed = _railed(med, em, ep)
  98     if expect_rail:
  99         ok = railed and (BETA_BOUNDS[1] - med) < 0.15
 100         detail = f"railed={railed}, gap-to-4={BETA_BOUNDS[1] - med:.3f}"
 101     else:
 102         # error side toward the truth, floored so a razor-thin posterior
 103         # cannot fail on numerical jitter
 104         sig = max(em if med > beta_true else ep, 0.01)
 105         ok = (abs(med - beta_true) <= 3.0 * sig) and not railed
 106         detail = f"|med-true|={abs(med - beta_true):.4f}, 3sig={3 * sig:.4f}, railed={railed}"
 107     return {
 108         "case": name,
 109         "beta_true": beta_true,
 110         "beta_median": med,
 111         "err_minus": em,
 112         "err_plus": ep,
 113         "alpha_derived": res["percentiles"]["alpha"]["median"],
 114         "log_evidence": res["log_evidence"],
 115         "ncall": res["ncall"],
 116         "expect_rail": expect_rail,
 117         "railed": railed,
 118         "ok": bool(ok),
 119         "detail": detail,
 120     }

1 """Compatibility-only historical joint scattering fitter.
   2 
   3 New dual-band dispersion and arrival-time inference uses
   4 ``radio_pipeline.fitting.fit_joint_event``. This module remains importable for
   5 historical-product reproduction and extracted-kernel parity checks.
   6 
   7 Joint two-telescope scattering fit (CHIME ~0.6 GHz + DSA ~1.4 GHz).
   8 
   9 Single-band M3 fits with alpha fixed = 4 give *inconsistent* tau_1ghz between
  10 CHIME and DSA for the same sightline (observed up to ~15x), which is only
  11 possible if the scattering index alpha != 4. A single band cannot separate
  12 alpha from tau (the tau-alpha degeneracy): tau(nu) = tau_1ghz * nu^-alpha, and
  13 one band fixes the product at its own frequency, not the slope.
  14 
  15 This module fits both bands simultaneously with a *shared* (tau_1ghz, alpha) and
  16 *per-telescope* (c0, t0, gamma, zeta, delta_dm). The ~1 GHz lever arm between
  17 the two bands measures alpha directly: the ratio tau_C/tau_D pins the slope,
  18 the shared tau_1ghz pins the normalization at 1 GHz.
  19 
  20 12-parameter vector (M3 both bands, alpha free):
  21 
  22     [tau_1ghz, alpha | c0_C, t0_C, gamma_C, zeta_C, ddm_C | c0_D, t0_D, gamma_D, zeta_D, ddm_D]
  23      ^shared sightline   ^CHIME intrinsic/timing            ^DSA intrinsic/timing
  24 
  25 Independent noise -> the joint log-likelihood is the sum of the two single-band
  26 Gaussian log-likelihoods (reuses the nch^2-fixed FRBModel.log_likelihood).
  27 
  28 zeta is kept per-telescope (not shared) in the default paths: intrinsic width is
  29 achromatic in principle, but the measured zeta also absorbs unmodelled per-band
  30 structure, so the conservative choice is to let each band fit its own. The alpha
  31 lever arm comes from the shared tau, independent of how zeta is treated.
  32 
  33 The ``shared_zeta`` path replaces the two per-band widths with ONE source width
  34 law zeta(nu) = zeta_1ghz * nu^x_zeta evaluated per channel across the full band
  35 (physically: the emission width belongs to the source, not the telescope, and
  36 pulsars show it evolving with frequency -- radius-to-frequency mapping). This
  37 makes the joint model a single coherent burst from the DSA top to the CHIME
  38 bottom (used by the unified full-band figure) at the cost of an x_zeta-alpha
  39 degeneracy: validate the x_zeta-alpha posterior covariance before trusting alpha.
  40 
  41 Usage
  42 -----
  43 ```python
  44 from burstfit_joint import fit_joint_scattering
  45 res = fit_joint_scattering(
  46     model_C=model_chime, init_C=init_chime,
  47     model_D=model_dsa,   init_D=init_dsa,
  48     alpha_bounds=(2.0, 6.0), nlive=600, nproc=8,
  49 )
  50 print(res["percentiles"]["alpha"], res["percentiles"]["tau_1ghz"])
  51 ```
  52 """
  53

  55 
  56 import hashlib
  57 import json
  58 import logging
  59 from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
  60 from dataclasses import replace
  61 from typing import Any
  62 
  63 import numpy as np
  64 from numpy.typing import NDArray
  65 
  66 from .burstfit import FRBModel, FRBParams, build_priors

  68     alpha_from_beta,
  69     beta_bounds_from_alpha_bounds,
  70     default_joint_beta_bounds,
  71 )
  72 
  73 log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  74 
  75 
  76 def _scientific_array_identity(array: NDArray) -> dict[str, Any]:
  77     canonical = np.ascontiguousarray(array)
  78     digest = hashlib.sha256()
  79     digest.update(canonical.dtype.str.encode("ascii"))
  80     digest.update(json.dumps(canonical.shape).encode("ascii"))
  81     digest.update(canonical.tobytes())
  82     return {
  83         "shape": list(canonical.shape),
  84         "dtype": canonical.dtype.str,

  86     }
  87 
  88 
  89 __all__ = [
  90     "fit_joint_scattering",
  91     "JOINT_PARAM_NAMES",
  92     "JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN",
  93     "JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN_GP",
  94     "JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN_MULTI",

  98 ]
  99 
 100 # Joint 12-vector layout. First two are the shared sightline params; the rest
 101 # are per-telescope (suffix _C = CHIME, _D = DSA).
 102 JOINT_PARAM_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = (
 103     "tau_1ghz",
 104     "beta",
 105     "c0_C",
 106     "t0_C",
 107     "gamma_C",
 108     "zeta_C",
 109     "delta_dm_C",

 117 _LOG_NAMES = frozenset({"tau_1ghz", "c0_C", "zeta_C", "c0_D", "zeta_D"})

 119 # Gain-marginalized 8-vector layout: the per-channel amplitude (gain) is
 120 # integrated analytically (matched-filter likelihood), so c0 and gamma drop out
 121 # of the sampled vector -- the gain absorbs the burst spectrum AND scintillation.
 122 # Only the temporal/scattering params remain. Lower-dim => easier sampling, and
 123 # the 2D residual whitens so chi2 becomes a valid goodness-of-fit gate.
 124 JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN: tuple[str, ...] = (
 125     "tau_1ghz",
 126     "beta",
 127     "t0_C",
 128     "zeta_C",
 129     "delta_dm_C",
 130     "t0_D",
 131     "zeta_D",
 132     "delta_dm_D",
 133 )

 136 # Gain-marginalized + scintillation-GP 10-vector layout. Adds a per-band
 137 # scintillation bandwidth Delta_nu_d (MHz). The flat per-channel gain prior is
 138 # replaced by a Lorentzian-ACF Gaussian process (see
 139 # FRBModel.log_likelihood_gain_marginal_gp); the smooth spectral envelope (mu)
 140 # and the GP amplitude (sigma_g) are profiled analytically, so ONLY Delta_nu_d
 141 # is added to the sampled vector (8 -> 10 dim).
 142 JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN_GP: tuple[str, ...] = (
 143     "tau_1ghz",
 144     "beta",
 145     "t0_C",
 146     "zeta_C",
 147     "delta_dm_C",
 148     "Delta_nu_d_C",
 149     "t0_D",
 150     "zeta_D",
 151     "delta_dm_D",
 152     "Delta_nu_d_D",
 153 )
 154 _LOG_NAMES_GAIN_GP = frozenset({"tau_1ghz", "zeta_C", "zeta_D", "Delta_nu_d_C", "Delta_nu_d_D"})

 156 # Gain-marginal + SHARED frequency-evolving intrinsic width 8-vector. The two
 157 # independent per-band widths (zeta_C, zeta_D) are replaced by ONE source law
 158 #
 159 #     zeta(nu) = zeta_1ghz * (nu / 1 GHz) ** x_zeta          (nu in GHz)
 160 #
 161 # evaluated per CHANNEL in each band. The width is a property of the source, not
 162 # the telescope; pulsars show it narrowing with frequency (radius-to-frequency
 163 # mapping, W ~ nu^-x, weak x ~ 0.1-0.4 -- Cordes 1978, Thorsett 1991), so the RFM
 164 # expectation is x_zeta < 0, with x_zeta = 0 the achromatic limit. Vector stays
 165 # 8-dim: (zeta_1ghz, x_zeta) replace (zeta_C, zeta_D); (t0, delta_dm) per band.
 166 #
 167 # CAVEAT (x_zeta-alpha degeneracy): a steeply negative x_zeta broadens low-freq
 168 # pulses the same way scattering (tau ~ nu^-alpha) does. The break is the tail
 169 # ASYMMETRY (one-sided exponential vs symmetric Gaussian) plus the ~1 GHz lever
 170 # arm; the wide x_zeta prior lets the data, not the prior, decide -- always check
 171 # the x_zeta-alpha posterior covariance before trusting alpha.

 173     "tau_1ghz",
 174     "beta",
 175     "zeta_1ghz",
 176     "x_zeta",
 177     "t0_C",
 178     "delta_dm_C",
 179     "t0_D",
 180     "delta_dm_D",
 181 )
 182 # x_zeta is a SIGNED power-law index -> uniform, not log. zeta_1ghz is log.
 183 _LOG_NAMES_GAIN_SZ = frozenset({"tau_1ghz", "zeta_1ghz"})

 186 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 187 # Multi-component (N>=1 pulses per band) gain-marginal layout.
 188 #
 189 # Each band carries n_comp temporal components; per component a (t0, zeta) pair
 190 # is sampled (suffix _C{i}/_D{i}, i=1..n_comp). (tau_1ghz, alpha) stay shared
 191 # across BOTH bands and ALL components -- one sightline, one scattering law.
 192 # delta_dm stays per-band (one cold-plasma column per telescope).
 193 #
 194 #   [tau_1ghz, alpha,
 195 #    t0_C1, zeta_C1, ..., t0_C{nC}, zeta_C{nC}, delta_dm_C,
 196 #    t0_D1, zeta_D1, ..., t0_D{nD}, zeta_D{nD}, delta_dm_D]
 197 #
 198 # n_comp=1 both bands -> 8-vector ordering IDENTICAL in content to
 199 # JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN (names differ by the _C1/_D1 suffix only); the existing
 200 # 8-vector path is untouched.
 201 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 202 def JOINT_PARAM_NAMES_GAIN_MULTI(n_C: int = 1, n_D: int = 1) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 203     """Param-name tuple for the N-component-per-band gain-marginal fit."""
 204     names: list[str] = ["tau_1ghz", "beta"]
 205     for i in range(1, int(n_C) + 1):
 206         names += [f"t0_C{i}", f"zeta_C{i}"]
 207     names.append("delta_dm_C")
 208     for i in range(1, int(n_D) + 1):
 209         names += [f"t0_D{i}", f"zeta_D{i}"]
 210     names.append("delta_dm_D")
 211     return tuple(names)

 214 def _gain_marginal_multi_band_impl(
 215     model: FRBModel,
 216     params_list: Sequence[FRBParams],
 217     model_keys: Sequence[str],
 218     s2: float | None = None,
 219     eig_rel_floor: float = 1e-6,
 220 ) -> tuple[float, dict[str, Any], NDArray[np.floating]]:
 221     """Per-channel linear-Gaussian gain-marginal evidence for ONE band.
 222 
 223     N temporal component kernels K_1..K_N per channel f; the per-component gains
 224     g ~ N(0, s2 I_N) carry the burst spectrum + scintillation. With noise var
 225     sigma_f^2 the per-channel marginal (Gaussian g integrated analytically) is
 226 
 227         M_ij = sum_t K_i,t K_j,t          (NxN, per channel)
 228         b_i  = sum_t d_t K_i,t            (N)
 229         S_dd = sum_t d_t^2
 230 
 231         ln Z_f = -0.5*[ S_dd/sigma^2 - b^T (M + (sigma^2/s2) I)^-1 b / sigma^2 ]
 232                  - 0.5*T*ln(2 pi sigma^2)                       (FULL data norm)
 233                  - 0.5*ln det( I_N + (s2/sigma^2) M )           (proper Occam)
 234 
 235     (The quadratic divisor is sigma^2, not sigma^4 -- verified against the brute
 236     Gaussian evidence d^T Sigma_d^-1 d, Sigma_d = sigma^2 I_T + s2 K K^T, via
 237     Woodbury; the SPEC's sigma^4 was a transcription slip.)
 238 
 239     The Occam term GROWS with N and with s2 -- the valid finite-variance penalty
 240     that the flat-improper version (-0.5 ln det M ~ +N ln s2 as s2->inf) got
 241     wrong, rewarding spurious merged components. As s2->inf, ln Z_f reduces to the
 242     flat F-stat profile -0.5*chi2min_f - 0.5*ln det M_f + 0.5*N*ln s2 (the last
 243     is a divergent param-INDEPENDENT constant that cancels in any ln Z DIFFERENCE).
 244 
 245     s2 is the gain-prior variance HYPERPARAMETER. If ``s2 is None`` it is profiled
 246     by 1-D ML on a SHARED-per-band value (state in the design notes); pass a float
 247     to fix it. Returns ``(lnZ, diag)`` with diagnostics:
 248     ``frac_culled`` (channels dropped by the eigenvalue guard), ``max_abs_g``
 249     (per component), ``s2``, ``n_supported`` (valid channels that kept the full
 250     N-component solve; ``frac_culled`` is normalized by all valid channels).
 251 
 252     Eigenvalue conditioning guard: a channel is culled when
 253     min eig(M_f) / max eig(M_f) < ``eig_rel_floor`` (near-degenerate kernels in
 254     the DAMAGE band where two components nearly merge -- M_f singular -> the full-N
 255     solve explodes |g|). A culled-but-SUPPORTED channel (real signal, collinear
 256     kernels) falls back to a rank-1 proper-prior evidence on its top eigenpair --
 257     NOT to the gain=0 baseline -- so a merge stays Occam-penalized (a reward at
 258     large fixed s2 otherwise; see the inline note). Only a genuinely unsupported
 259     channel (emax ~ 0, no signal) gets the gain=0 baseline
 260     -0.5 S_dd/sigma^2 - 0.5 T ln(2 pi sigma^2). ``frac_culled`` counts all
 261     not-full-rank-N channels (rank-1 fallback + unsupported).
 262     """
 263     if model.data is None or model.noise_std is None:
 264         raise RuntimeError("need data + noise_std")
 265     valid = model.valid
 266     if valid is None or not np.any(valid):
 267         return (
 268             -np.inf,
 269             {"frac_culled": 1.0, "max_abs_g": None, "s2": s2, "n_supported": 0},
 270             np.empty((0, len(params_list))),
 271         )
 272 
 273     Ks = np.stack(
 274         [
 275             model(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), mk, freq_subset=valid)
 276             for p, mk in zip(params_list, model_keys, strict=True)
 277         ]
 278     )  # (N, F, T)
 279     N, F, T = Ks.shape
 280     d = model.data[valid]  # (F, T)
 281     sig = np.clip(model.noise_std[valid], 1e-9, None)  # (F,)
 282     var = sig**2  # (F,)
 283 
 284     S_dd = np.einsum("ft,ft->f", d, d)  # (F,)
 285     b = np.einsum("nft,ft->fn", Ks, d)  # (F, N)
 286     M = np.einsum("nft,mft->fnm", Ks, Ks)  # (F, N, N)
 287 
 288     # Eigenvalue conditioning guard (per channel). M is symmetric PSD. We keep the
 289     # eigenVECTORS (eigh, not eigvalsh) so a culled channel can fall back to its
 290     # rank-1 top-eigenpair proper evidence instead of the gain=0 baseline -- see
 291     # below for why that distinction is load-bearing.
 292     evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(M)  # (F, N) asc, (F, N, N)
 293     emax = evals[:, -1]
 294     emin = evals[:, 0]
 295     supported = emax > 1e-30  # any signal at all
 296     cond_ok = np.zeros(F, dtype=bool)
 297     cond_ok[supported] = (
 298         emin[supported] / np.where(emax[supported] > 0, emax[supported], 1.0) >= eig_rel_floor
 299     )
 300     ok = supported & cond_ok  # well-conditioned channels
 301     # Culled-but-supported channels: kernels collinear (a near-merge), but there
 302     # IS signal. Route them to a rank-1 model on the top eigenvector (one
 303     # effective kernel), NOT to gain=0. This matters because at large fixed s2 the
 304     # gain=0 baseline -0.5 S_dd/var - 0.5 T ln(2pi var) sits ABOVE the proper N=1
 305     # lnZ (which carries the divergent +0.5 ln(s2/var) Occam per channel), so
 306     # culling-to-baseline would REWARD a degenerate merge by ~+0.5 F ln(s2/var)
 307     # (e.g. +676 nats at s2=1e8) -- reintroducing the very bug the prior fixes for
 308     # any caller that bypasses the ordered transform. The rank-1 fallback is
 309     # continuous with the N=1 proper model, so the merge is a penalty, not a reward.
 310     cull = supported & ~cond_ok  # (F,)
 311     eye = np.eye(N)
 312 
 313     def _lnZ_at(s2v: float) -> tuple[float, NDArray[np.floating]]:
 314         # gain=0 baseline only for genuinely unsupported (no-signal) channels.
 315         base = -0.5 * S_dd / var - 0.5 * T * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * var)
 316         lnZ_f = base.copy()
 317         g_all = np.zeros((F, N))
 318         if np.any(ok):
 319             Mok = M[ok]  # (G, N, N)
 320             bok = b[ok]  # (G, N)
 321             varok = var[ok]  # (G,)
 322             ridge = (varok / s2v)[:, None, None] * eye[None]
 323             A = Mok + ridge  # (G, N, N)
 324             g = np.linalg.solve(A, bok[:, :, None])[:, :, 0]  # (G, N), the MAP gain
 325             quad = np.einsum("gn,gn->g", g, bok)  # b^T A^-1 b
 326             # ln det( I + (s2/var) M ) via eigvals of M (per channel).
 327             ev_ok = evals[ok]  # (G, N)
 328             logdet_occam = np.sum(
 329                 np.log1p((s2v / varok)[:, None] * np.clip(ev_ok, 0.0, None)),
 330                 axis=1,
 331             )  # (G,)
 332             lnZ_ok = (
 333                 -0.5 * (S_dd[ok] / varok - quad / varok)
 334                 - 0.5 * T * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * varok)
 335                 - 0.5 * logdet_occam
 336             )
 337             lnZ_f[ok] = lnZ_ok
 338             g_all[ok] = g
 339         if np.any(cull):
 340             # rank-1 proper evidence on the top eigenpair (scalar effective kernel
 341             # with norm^2 = emax, projected data b.v_top). MAP gain along v_top is
 342             # then distributed back onto the components via v_top for diagnostics.
 343             emx = emax[cull]  # (C,)
 344             vtop = evecs[cull][:, :, -1]  # (C, N)
 345             bproj = np.einsum("cn,cn->c", b[cull], vtop)  # (C,)
 346             varc = var[cull]  # (C,)
 347             Ac = emx + varc / s2v
 348             gc = bproj / Ac  # (C,) scalar MAP along v_top
 349             quadc = gc * bproj
 350             occ_c = np.log1p((s2v / varc) * np.clip(emx, 0.0, None))
 351             lnZ_f[cull] = (
 352                 -0.5 * (S_dd[cull] / varc - quadc / varc)
 353                 - 0.5 * T * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * varc)
 354                 - 0.5 * occ_c
 355             )
 356             g_all[cull] = gc[:, None] * vtop  # (C, N)
 357         return float(np.sum(lnZ_f)), g_all
 358 
 359     if s2 is None:
 360         # 1-D ML over log s2, range anchored on the data scale: var(ahat) where
 361         # ahat=b/diag(M) is the matched-filter gain ~ sets the signal amplitude.
 362         diagM = np.einsum("fnn->fn", M)
 363         with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
 364             ahat = np.where(diagM > 0, b / np.where(diagM > 0, diagM, 1.0), 0.0)
 365         scale = max(float(np.var(ahat[ok])) if np.any(ok) else 1.0, 1e-12)
 366         from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
 367 
 368         lo, hi = np.log(scale) - 18.0, np.log(scale) + 18.0
 369         res = minimize_scalar(
 370             lambda ls: -_lnZ_at(float(np.exp(ls)))[0],
 371             bounds=(lo, hi),
 372             method="bounded",
 373             options={"xatol": 1e-3},
 374         )
 375         s2_used = float(np.exp(res.x))
 376     else:
 377         s2_used = float(s2)
 378 
 379     lnZ, g_all = _lnZ_at(s2_used)
 380     max_abs_g = [float(np.max(np.abs(g_all[:, i]))) if F else 0.0 for i in range(N)]
 381     # NB: n_supported and frac_culled use DIFFERENT denominators. n_supported counts
 382     # only well-conditioned (full-rank-N) channels (`ok`), whereas frac_culled =
 383     # mean(~ok) also counts rank-1-fallback channels as culled -- so in general
 384     # n_supported != (1 - frac_culled) * F.
 385     diag = {
 386         "frac_culled": float(np.mean(~ok)),
 387         "max_abs_g": max_abs_g,
 388         "s2": s2_used,
 389         "n_supported": int(np.count_nonzero(ok)),
 390     }
 391     return (lnZ if np.isfinite(lnZ) else -np.inf), diag, g_all
 392

 430 def _dnu_d_bounds(freq_GHz: NDArray[np.floating]) -> tuple[float, float]:
 431     """Log-uniform Delta_nu_d prior bounds (MHz) from a band's freq axis.
 432 
 433     Resolvable range: lower = 0.3 * channel width (below this the GP is
 434     unresolved and degrades to a flat upper limit); upper = band / 3 (a few
 435     scintles minimum). Derived per band from the data, not hardcoded.
 436     """
 437     nu = np.asarray(freq_GHz, dtype=float)
 438     chan_w_MHz = float(np.median(np.abs(np.diff(nu)))) * 1.0e3
 439     band_MHz = float(nu.max() - nu.min()) * 1.0e3
 440     return (0.3 * chan_w_MHz, band_MHz / 3.0)

 577 def _clamp_t0_priors_to_window(
 578     spec: list[tuple[str, tuple[float, float], bool]],
 579     model_C: FRBModel,
 580     model_D: FRBModel,
 581 ) -> list[tuple[str, tuple[float, float], bool]]:
 582     """Bound every component t0 prior to its band's fitted window [time.min, time.max].
 583 
 584     build_priors' default t0 window is init.t0 +/- 2*max(tau_1ghz, 10.0) = +/- 20 ms
 585     (the max(...,10) floor), untethered from the ~ms fitted window, so a global sampler
 586     can place components far outside the data window where the gain marginal exploits
 587     their kernels as per-channel baseline dof (zach fine-pair ghost components,
 588     COMPONENT_COUNT_LADDER_AUDIT 2026-07-18). This clamps t0_C* to model_C's window and
 589     t0_D* to model_D's window: a component must live in the window the count test is
 590     defined on (the dual of the window-contains-all-candidates rule). Non-t0 entries and
 591     already-in-window bounds are unchanged; matches t0_C / t0_D (single) and
 592     t0_C{i} / t0_D{i} (multi) by prefix.
 593     """
 594     tC = np.asarray(model_C.time, dtype=float)
 595     tD = np.asarray(model_D.time, dtype=float)
 596     win_C = (float(tC.min()), float(tC.max()))
 597     win_D = (float(tD.min()), float(tD.max()))
 598     out: list[tuple[str, tuple[float, float], bool]] = []
 599     for name, (lo, hi), is_log in spec:
 600         if name.startswith("t0_C"):
 601             lo, hi = max(lo, win_C[0]), min(hi, win_C[1])
 602         elif name.startswith("t0_D"):
 603             lo, hi = max(lo, win_D[0]), min(hi, win_D[1])
 604         out.append((name, (lo, hi), is_log))
 605     return out

 608 class _JointPriorTransform:
 609     """Picklable unit-cube -> parameter transform for the 12-vector.
 610 
 611     Module-level callable (not a closure) so dynesty.pool can ship it to workers.
 612     Log-uniform on the flagged positive params, uniform on the rest.
 613     """
 614 
 615     def __init__(self, spec: list[tuple[str, tuple[float, float], bool]]):
 616         self.lo = np.array([s[1][0] for s in spec], dtype=float)
 617         self.hi = np.array([s[1][1] for s in spec], dtype=float)
 618         # only log-sample where flagged AND both bounds strictly positive
 619         self.is_log = np.array([bool(s[2] and s[1][0] > 0 and s[1][1] > 0) for s in spec])
 620         # precompute log-bounds with safe placeholders (log(1)=0) on linear axes
 621         self._loglo = np.log(np.where(self.is_log, self.lo, 1.0))
 622         self._loghi = np.log(np.where(self.is_log, self.hi, 1.0))
 623 
 624     def __call__(self, u: NDArray[np.floating]) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 625         lin = self.lo + u * (self.hi - self.lo)
 626         logu = np.exp(self._loglo + u * (self._loghi - self._loglo))
 627         return np.where(self.is_log, logu, lin)

 630 class _JointPriorTransformOrdered(_JointPriorTransform):
 631     """Ordered + min-separation transform for the multi-component vector.
 632 
 633     Within each band the per-component t0 group is SORTED ascending (breaks the
 634     label-swap degeneracy: N! identical posterior modes collapse to one), then
 635     forced to obey t0_{i+1} - t0_i >= dt_min. The min-separation is enforced by
 636     re-mapping the unit cube of the t0 group onto the simplex
 637     {t0_1 <= ... <= t0_N, gaps >= dt_min} so EVERY cube point lands in the
 638     feasible region (no rejected volume, no -inf from the transform -- dynesty's
 639     cube map must stay total). A cube whose feasible width
 640     (hi - lo - (N-1)*dt_min) is <= 0 collapses the group to a single point and
 641     the likelihood (degenerate kernels) is culled by the eigenvalue guard, so the
 642     merge is penalized by the Occam term, not rewarded -- which is the whole fix.
 643 
 644     dt_min defaults to a few channel time-samples (>= the kernel can resolve); the
 645     caller passes the band time grids so it is data-derived, not hardcoded. dt_min may
 646     be a scalar (one floor broadcast to every group) or one value per t0 group, so each
 647     band's components are bound by THAT band's time resolution.
 648     """
 649 
 650     def __init__(self, spec, t0_groups, dt_min):
 651         super().__init__(spec)
 652         # t0_groups: list of index arrays into the param vector, one per band,
 653         # giving the positions of that band's t0_C1..t0_C{n} (already ascending).
 654         self.t0_groups = [np.asarray(g, dtype=int) for g in t0_groups]
 655         # dt_min: scalar -> broadcast to every group; sequence -> one floor per group
 656         # (per-band). Stored as a plain list[float] (pickles to dynesty pools).
 657         if np.ndim(dt_min) == 0:
 658             self.dt_min = [float(dt_min)] * len(self.t0_groups)
 659         else:
 660             self.dt_min = [float(d) for d in dt_min]
 661             if len(self.dt_min) != len(self.t0_groups):
 662                 raise ValueError(
 663                     f"dt_min sequence length {len(self.dt_min)} != {len(self.t0_groups)} t0 groups"
 664                 )
 665 
 666     def __call__(self, u: NDArray[np.floating]) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 667         x = super().__call__(u)
 668         for grp, dtm in zip(self.t0_groups, self.dt_min, strict=True):
 669             n = grp.size
 670             if n < 2:
 671                 continue
 672             lo = self.lo[grp[0]]
 673             hi = self.hi[grp[0]]
 674             # Feasible width after reserving (n-1)*dt_min of separation.
 675             usable = hi - lo - (n - 1) * dtm
 676             uu = np.sort(u[grp])  # n sorted unit-cube coords -> ordered
 677             if usable > 0:
 678                 # place n ordered points in [0, usable], then add cumulative dt_min
 679                 pts = lo + uu * usable + np.arange(n) * dtm
 680             else:
 681                 # band too narrow for n separated comps -> collapse (culled by guard)
 682                 pts = np.full(n, lo + uu.mean() * (hi - lo))
 683             x[grp] = pts
 684         return x

 783 class _JointLogLikelihoodGainSharedZeta:
 784     """Joint gain-marginal log-L with ONE frequency-evolving intrinsic width.
 785 
 786     8-vector theta = [tau, beta, zeta_1ghz, x_zeta, t0_C, ddm_C, t0_D, ddm_D].
 787     Per band zeta(nu) = zeta_1ghz * nu**x_zeta is evaluated on that band's FULL
 788     channel axis (nu in GHz; model.freq ascending) and passed as a per-channel
 789     ARRAY into FRBParams.zeta. The kernel builds sig = hypot(sig_dm, zeta) on the
 790     same full axis before masking to self.valid, so the zeta array MUST be full
 791     length (not pre-subset) -- it is, by construction. The per-channel amplitude
 792     is still integrated out (log_likelihood_gain_marginal), so c0/gamma are not
 793     sampled. One source width law spans both telescopes.
 794     """
 795 
 796     def __init__(self, model_C: FRBModel, model_D: FRBModel):
 797         self.model_C = model_C
 798         self.model_D = model_D
 799 
 800     @staticmethod
 801     def _band_ll(
 802         model: FRBModel, tau: float, beta: float, z1: float, x: float, t0: float, ddm: float
 803     ) -> float:
 804         zeta_nu = z1 * np.asarray(model.freq, dtype=float) ** x  # full channel axis
 805         p = FRBParams(c0=1.0, t0=t0, gamma=0.0, zeta=zeta_nu, tau_1ghz=tau, beta=beta, delta_dm=ddm)

 809         tau, beta, z1, x = (float(theta[i]) for i in range(4))

 811             self.model_C, tau, beta, z1, x, float(theta[4]), float(theta[5])
 812         ) + self._band_ll(self.model_D, tau, beta, z1, x, float(theta[6]), float(theta[7]))

 121 def analytic_gaussian_exp_convolution(t, mu, sig, tau):
 122     """
 123     Analytic convolution of a Gaussian G(t; mu, sig) and an exponential E(t; tau).
 124 
 125     This uses the erfcx-based stable formulation:
 126     f(t) = (1/2*tau) * exp(-(t-mu)^2 / (2*sig^2)) * erfcx(sig/(sqrt(2)*tau) - (t-mu)/(sqrt(2)*sig))
 127 
 128     Stability:
 129     If tau -> 0 (scattering is negligible compared to smearing), this returns G(t).
 130     If sig -> 0 (smearing is negligible compared to scattering), this returns E(t).
 131     """
 132     if t.ndim == 1:
 133         t = t[None, :]
 134 
 135     # Pre-calculate common terms
 136     t_minus_mu = t - mu
 137 
 138     # --- STABILITY GUARD: Gaussian Limit ---
 139     # If tau is extremely small relative to sig, convolution is just the Gaussian.
 140     # This prevents numerical overflow in erfcx(b) / inv_tau when tau -> 0.
 141     is_gauss = (tau < 1e-9) | (sig > 100 * tau)
 142 
 143     # Standard Gaussian part (unnormalized)
 144     gauss_exp = np.exp(-0.5 * (t_minus_mu / sig) ** 2)
 145 
 146     # Initialize result with Gaussian limit
 147     # f(t) = (1/sqrt(2pi)sig) * exp(-0.5*(t-mu/sig)^2)
 148     res = (1.0 / (np.sqrt(2.0 * np.pi) * sig)) * gauss_exp
 149 
 150     # Only evaluate the erfcx part where it is NOT a pure Gaussian
 151     # This avoids NaNs from inf * 0 in the deep tails.
 152     mask = ~is_gauss.squeeze()
 153     if np.any(mask):
 154         # We need to handle masks carefully for 2D broadcast
 155         # mask is (nfreq,), results are (nfreq, ntime)
 156         inv_tau_m = 1.0 / tau[mask]
 157         t_m = t_minus_mu[mask]
 158         sig_m = sig[mask]
 159 
 160         b = (sig_m / (np.sqrt(2.0) * tau[mask])) - (t_m / (np.sqrt(2.0) * sig_m))
 161 
 162         # --- NUMERICAL STABILITY FIX ---
 163         # When b is large negative (deep tail or tiny sigma), erfcx(b) overflows
 164         # and gauss_exp underflows. The product should be finite.
 165         # Use asymptotic form: gauss_exp * erfcx(b) ~= 2 * exp(k^2 - 2kx)
 166         # where k = sig/(sqrt(2)*tau) and x = (t-mu)/(sqrt(2)*sig)
 167         # k^2 - 2kx = 0.5*(sig/tau)^2 - (t-mu)/tau
 168 
 169         # Threshold for erfcx overflow (approx -26 for float64)
 170         safe_mask = b > -25.0
 171 
 172         res_m = np.zeros_like(b)
 173         inv_tau_expanded = np.broadcast_to(inv_tau_m, b.shape)
 174 
 175         # Safe region: use standard formula
 176         if np.any(safe_mask):
 177             g_exp = gauss_exp[mask]
 178             res_m[safe_mask] = (
 179                 (0.5 * inv_tau_expanded[safe_mask]) * g_exp[safe_mask] * erfcx(b[safe_mask])
 180             )
 181 
 182         # Overflow region: use asymptotic approximation
 183         # res_m = (1/tau) * exp(0.5*(sig/tau)^2 - (t-mu)/tau)
 184         overflow_mask = ~safe_mask
 185         if np.any(overflow_mask):
 186             # k^2 term: 0.5 * (sig/tau)^2
 187             k2 = 0.5 * (sig_m / tau[mask]) ** 2
 188             # -2kx term: -(t-mu)/tau
 189             minus_2kx = -t_m / tau[mask]
 190             exponent = k2 + minus_2kx
 191 
 192             res_m[overflow_mask] = inv_tau_expanded[overflow_mask] * np.exp(exponent[overflow_mask])
 193 
 194         # Replace NaNs (if any remain in deep tails) with 0
 195         np.nan_to_num(res_m, copy=False, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
 196 
 197         res[mask] = res_m
 198 
 199     return res

 203     """

 207     negligible inner scale, the thin-screen PBF is exponential at small lag and
 208     develops a heavy power-law tail at large lag (Cordes review sec 11.2, after
 209     Ostashov & Shishov 1978; Lee & Jokipii 1975; Lambert & Rickett 1999):
 210 
 211         p(s) ~ exp(-s)                 for s <= s_c
 212         p(s) ~ (s / s_c)^(-beta/2)     for s >  s_c     [continuous at s_c]
 213 
 214     with s = lag / tau and the crossover s_c = 2 ln(2 / (4 - beta)) from the same
 215     review. As beta -> 4, s_c -> infinity and the PBF reduces to the pure
 216     exponential e^{-s}, recovering analytic_gaussian_exp_convolution in shape (the
 217     FFT path leaves a ~0.5-sample time-registration offset vs the closed form, but
 218     that is fully degenerate with the free t0 and so cancels in any fit/evidence);
 219     Kolmogorov is beta = 11/3 (tail slope -11/6). The tail is normalizable for
 220     beta > 2 (the mean delay still diverges for beta < 4, per the review).
 221 
 222     Returns an area-normalized density on the time grid (continuous integral ~ 1),
 223     matching analytic_gaussian_exp_convolution so the exp-vs-power-law evidence is
 224     on the same amplitude footing. Computed by zero-padded FFT linear convolution.
 225     """
 226     if t.ndim == 1:
 227         t = t[None, :]
 228     T = t.shape[1]
 229     dt = t[0, 1] - t[0, 0]
 230 
 231     # Area-normalized Gaussian (same convention as the exp / M0,M1 paths)
 232     g = (1.0 / (np.sqrt(2.0 * np.pi) * sig)) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - mu) / sig) ** 2)
 233 
 234     # One-sided PBF on a causal lag grid. beta clipped to the integrable,
 235     # non-degenerate open interval (2, 4); s_c floored so the tail term never
 236     # divides by zero (the s=0 value lands in the exp branch regardless).
 237     beta = float(np.clip(beta, 2.01, 3.99))
 238     s_c = max(2.0 * np.log(2.0 / (4.0 - beta)), 1e-3)
 239     lag = (np.arange(T) * dt)[None, :]
 240     s = lag / tau
 241     h = np.where(
 242         s <= s_c,
 243         np.exp(-s),
 244         np.exp(-s_c) * (np.maximum(s, s_c) / s_c) ** (-0.5 * beta),
 245     )
 246     h = h / np.clip(h.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) * dt, 1e-30, None)
 247 
 248     # *dt makes the discrete linear convolution the sampled continuous one, so
 249     # the returned profile integrates to ~1 like analytic_gaussian_exp_convolution.
 250     # A pocketfft-fast transform length (composite of primes <=11) avoids the
 251     # O(N^2) fallback when 2*T has a large prime factor (e.g. T=257 prime ->
 252     # 2*T=514=2*257 -> 525); the result is exact because L >= 2*T still captures
 253     # the full linear convolution and the extra tail is dropped by the [:T] slice.
 254     L = _next_fast_len(2 * T)
 255     conv = np.fft.irfft(np.fft.rfft(g, L, axis=1) * np.fft.rfft(h, L, axis=1), L, axis=1)
 256     return conv[:, :T] * dt

 506 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 507 # Gaussian-process spectral marginal (diffractive scintillation)
 508 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 509 def _gp_amplitude_logL(
 510     ahat: NDArray[np.floating],
 511     v: NDArray[np.floating],
 512     freq_MHz: NDArray[np.floating],
 513     delta_nu_d_MHz: float,
 514     mu_degree: int = 1,
 515     sigma_g2: float | None = None,
 516 ) -> tuple[float, float, NDArray[np.floating], float]:
 517     """Spectral GP marginal over the matched-filter gain estimates `ahat`.
 518 
 519     Diffractive scintillation makes the per-channel gain estimates correlated in
 520     frequency with a Lorentzian ACF of half-width `delta_nu_d` (the scintillation
 521     bandwidth). We model the gain-estimate vector as
 522 
 523         ahat ~ N(mu, Sigma),  Sigma = sigma_g^2 C(delta_nu_d) + diag(v)
 524         C[f,f'] = 1 / (1 + ((nu_f - nu_f') / delta_nu_d)^2)   (unit-amplitude Lorentzian)
 525         mu = X beta  (smooth intrinsic envelope, Vandermonde of centred+scaled freq)
 526 
 527     mu is profiled by generalized least squares (flat prior on beta -> the
 528     +0.5 ln|X^T Sigma^-1 X| Jacobian term), and sigma_g^2 by 1-D maximum
 529     likelihood unless overridden via `sigma_g2`.
 530 
 531     Returns ``(logL_amp, sigma_g2_ml, mu, modulation_index)`` where ``logL_amp``
 532     is the SPECTRAL block only (the temporal -0.5 sum chi2min is added by the
 533     caller). It comprises
 534 
 535         -0.5 (ahat-mu)^T Sigma^-1 (ahat-mu)      [GP residual]
 536         -0.5 ln|Sigma|                            [GP Occam, generalizes -0.5 ln S_kk]
 537         +0.5 ln|X^T Sigma^-1 X|                   [GLS mu-profiling Jacobian]
 538         -0.5 sum_f ln(2 pi v_f)                   [ahat|g white-noise normalizer]
 539 
 540     Numerics: whiten the correlation by the diagonal, M = D^{-1/2} C D^{-1/2}
 541     = Q L Q^T (one symmetric eigendecomposition per call), then for any sigma_g^2
 542     both ln|Sigma| = sum ln v + sum ln(sigma_g^2 L_k + 1) and the quadratic /
 543     GLS forms are O(n) in the rotated basis. The sigma_g^2 sweep therefore costs
 544     one O(n^3) eigendecomposition + O(n) per inner evaluation (cf. derivation
 545     notes / SPEC.profile_strategy).
 546     """
 547     ahat = np.asarray(ahat, dtype=float)
 548     v = np.clip(np.asarray(v, dtype=float), 1e-30, None)
 549     nu = np.asarray(freq_MHz, dtype=float)
 550     n = ahat.size
 551 
 552     # Lorentzian correlation on live channels (unit amplitude).
 553     dnu = nu[:, None] - nu[None, :]
 554     C = 1.0 / (1.0 + (dnu / float(delta_nu_d_MHz)) ** 2)
 555 
 556     # Whiten by the noise diagonal: M = D^{-1/2} C D^{-1/2} = Q L Q^T.
 557     dinv_sqrt = 1.0 / np.sqrt(v)
 558     M = (dinv_sqrt[:, None] * C) * dinv_sqrt[None, :]
 559     M = 0.5 * (M + M.T)  # symmetrize against round-off before eigh
 560     L, Q = eigh(M)
 561     L = np.clip(L, 0.0, None)  # C is PSD; clip tiny negative round-off
 562 
 563     # Rotate the data and the design matrix into the eigenbasis ONCE.
 564     # Vandermonde of centred+scaled freq keeps X^T Sigma^-1 X well-conditioned.
 565     span = float(nu.max() - nu.min())
 566     nu_c = (nu - nu.mean()) / (span if span > 0 else 1.0)
 567     X = np.vander(nu_c, N=int(mu_degree) + 1, increasing=True)  # (n, p+1)
 568     a_w = Q.T @ (dinv_sqrt * ahat)  # Q^T D^{-1/2} ahat
 569     X_w = Q.T @ (dinv_sqrt[:, None] * X)  # Q^T D^{-1/2} X   (n, p+1)
 570     logdet_v = float(np.sum(np.log(v)))
 571 
 572     def _profile_mu(s2: float) -> tuple[NDArray[np.floating], NDArray[np.floating]]:
 573         """GLS beta and rotated residual z = Q^T D^{-1/2} (ahat - mu) at sigma_g^2=s2."""
 574         d_eig = s2 * L + 1.0  # eigenvalues of D^{-1/2} Sigma D^{-1/2}
 575         inv_d = 1.0 / d_eig
 576         # X^T Sigma^-1 X = X_w^T diag(inv_d) X_w ; X^T Sigma^-1 ahat = X_w^T diag(inv_d) a_w
 577         XtSiX = (X_w * inv_d[:, None]).T @ X_w
 578         XtSia = (X_w * inv_d[:, None]).T @ a_w
 579         beta = np.linalg.solve(XtSiX, XtSia)
 580         z = a_w - X_w @ beta  # rotated residual
 581         return beta, z
 582 
 583     def _neglogL_s2(log_s2: float, return_full: bool = False):
 584         s2 = float(np.exp(log_s2))
 585         beta, z = _profile_mu(s2)
 586         d_eig = s2 * L + 1.0
 587         quad = float(np.sum(z * z / d_eig))
 588         logdet_sigma = logdet_v + float(np.sum(np.log(d_eig)))
 589         # GLS Jacobian (flat prior on beta): +0.5 ln|X^T Sigma^-1 X|
 590         inv_d = 1.0 / d_eig
 591         XtSiX = (X_w * inv_d[:, None]).T @ X_w
 592         sgn, logdet_XtSiX = np.linalg.slogdet(XtSiX)
 593         jac = 0.5 * logdet_XtSiX if sgn > 0 else -1e30
 594         logL = -0.5 * quad - 0.5 * logdet_sigma + jac - 0.5 * (n * np.log(2.0 * np.pi) + logdet_v)
 595         if return_full:
 596             return logL, beta, s2
 597         return -logL
 598 
 599     if sigma_g2 is not None:
 600         # Caller-forced amplitude (used by the decorrelated-wide flat-limit test).
 601         logL, beta, s2_ml = _neglogL_s2(np.log(float(sigma_g2)), return_full=True)
 602     else:
 603         # Bounded 1-D ML over log(sigma_g^2). Golden-section cannot diverge near
 604         # the (non-convex) unresolved boundary, unlike Newton. Range anchored on
 605         # the data scale: median(v) sets the noise floor, var(ahat) the ceiling.
 606         from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
 607 
 608         med_v = float(np.median(v))
 609         scale = max(med_v, float(np.var(ahat)), 1e-30)
 610         lo, hi = np.log(scale) - 18.0, np.log(scale) + 18.0
 611         res = minimize_scalar(
 612             _neglogL_s2, bounds=(lo, hi), method="bounded", options={"xatol": 1e-3}
 613         )
 614         logL, beta, s2_ml = _neglogL_s2(res.x, return_full=True)
 615 
 616     mu = X @ beta
 617     # Modulation index of the (envelope-removed) gain estimates: std of the
 618     # fractional residual. Independent sub-resolution scintillation probe.
 619     with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
 620         frac = (ahat - mu) / np.where(np.abs(mu) > 1e-30, mu, np.nan)
 621     mod_index = float(np.nanstd(frac)) if np.any(np.isfinite(frac)) else float("nan")
 622     return float(logL), float(s2_ml), mu, mod_index

 630     Forward model + (Gaussian) log-likelihood for a dynamic spectrum.

 632 
 633     def __init__(
 634         self,
 635         time: NDArray[np.floating],

 637         *,
 638         data: NDArray[np.floating] | None = None,
