 643         off_pulse: slice | Sequence[int] | None = None,
 644     ) -> None:
 645         self.time = np.asarray(time, dtype=float)
 646         self.freq = np.asarray(freq, dtype=float)
 647         self.df_MHz = float(df_MHz)
 648 
 649         if data is not None:
 650             self.data = np.asarray(data, dtype=float)
 651             if self.data.shape != (self.freq.size, self.time.size):
 652                 raise ValueError("data must have shape (nfreq, ntime)")

 654             self.data = None
 655 
 656         self.dm_init = float(dm_init)
 657         self.beta = float(beta)
 658 
 659         if not np.allclose(np.diff(self.time), self.time[1] - self.time[0]):
 660             raise ValueError("time axis must be uniform")
 661         self.dt = self.time[1] - self.time[0]
 662 
 663         # NOTE: the pre-ADR-0006 FLITS_PBF / FLITS_PBF_BETA env selector is gone.
 664         # The PBF family is coupled to the sampled turbulence index: __call__
 665         # dispatches on p.beta alone (exp at beta -> 4, power-law tail below),
 666         # per docs/adr/0006 and its rationale addendum (an exponential PBF is
 667         # uniquely beta = 4, hence alpha = 4).
 668 
 669         if noise_std is None and self.data is not None:
 670             self.noise_std = self._estimate_noise(off_pulse)
 671         else:
 672             self.noise_std = noise_std
 673 
 674         # Pre-calculate validity mask (exclude dead channels and NaNs)
 675         if self.data is not None and self.noise_std is not None:
 676             self.valid = (self.noise_std > 1e-9) & (np.isfinite(np.nanmean(self.data, axis=1)))
 677         else:
 678             self.valid = None

 680     def _dispersion_delay(
 681         self, dm_err: float = 0.0, ref_freq: float | None = None
 682     ) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 683         if ref_freq is None:
 684             ref_freq = self.freq.max()
 685         return DM_DELAY_MS * dm_err * (self.freq**-self.beta - ref_freq**-self.beta)
 686 
 687     # ## REFACTOR ##: Smearing calculation is now more explicit.
 688     def _smearing_sigma(self, dm: float, zeta: float) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 689         """Total Gaussian width from intrinsic pulse width (zeta) and
 690         intra-channel DM smearing.
 691 
 692         Intra-channel smearing is the dispersive delay across ONE *native* channel
 693         at the dedispersion DM, so self.df_MHz must be the NATIVE channel width
 694         (io.py sets it from telescope.df_MHz_raw, not the downsampled width). It is
 695         a boxcar of full width dt_DM; modelled as a Gaussian its variance-matched
 696         sigma is dt_DM/sqrt(12). Pass dm=0 for coherently-dedispersed data (CHIME,
 697         smearing removed) and the catalog DM for incoherently-dedispersed data (DSA).
 698         """
 699         # dt_DM (ms) = 8.3e-3 * DM(pc cm^-3) * df_MHz(native) * nu_GHz^-3  (Lorimer & Kramer 2005)
 700         dt_dm = DM_SMEAR_MS * dm * self.df_MHz * (self.freq**-3.0)
 701         sig_dm = dt_dm / np.sqrt(12.0)  # uniform (boxcar) -> Gaussian-equivalent sigma
 702         return np.hypot(sig_dm, zeta)

 704     def _estimate_noise(self, off_pulse):
 705         if self.data is None:
 706             return None
 707         if off_pulse is None:
 708             q = self.time.size // 4
 709             idx = np.r_[0:q, -q:0]
 710         else:
 711             idx = np.asarray(off_pulse)
 712 
 713         # Ensure indices are within bounds
 714         idx = idx[idx < self.data.shape[1]]
 715 
 716         mad = np.median(
 717             np.abs(self.data[:, idx] - np.median(self.data[:, idx], axis=1, keepdims=True)),
 718             axis=1,
 719         )
 720         return 1.4826 * mad  # Do not clip to 1e-6, allow 0 for dead channels

 722     def __call__(
 723         self, p: FRBParams, model_key: str = "M3", freq_subset: NDArray[np.bool_] | None = None
 724     ) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 725         """Return model dynamic spectrum for parameters *p*.
 726 
 727         Args:
 728             p: Parameters
 729             model_key: Model variant
 730             freq_subset: Optional boolean mask of frequencies to evaluate.
 731                          If None, evaluates all frequencies.
 732         """
 733         if freq_subset is None:
 734             freq = self.freq
 735         else:
 736             freq = self.freq[freq_subset]
 737 
 738         n_freq = freq.size
 739         n_time = self.time.size
 740 
 741         ref_freq = np.median(self.freq)  # Keep global ref_freq for consistency
 742         amp = p.c0 * (freq / ref_freq) ** p.gamma
 743 
 744         # Dispersion delay
 745         dd_full = self._dispersion_delay(p.delta_dm)
 746         if freq_subset is None:
 747             mu = p.t0 + dd_full[:, None]
 748         else:
 749             mu = p.t0 + dd_full[freq_subset, None]
 750 
 751         # Intra-channel smearing scales with the TRUE DM offset from the de-smear
 752         # baseline: dm_init (the DM the data was dedispersed at) plus the fitted
 753         # residual delta_dm. With dm_init=0 in the configs, omitting delta_dm here
 754         # left a fitted residual DM (e.g. CHIME delta_dm~4.7) with zero modelled
 755         # smearing, so its real smearing leaked into zeta/tau and biased alpha
 756         # (Codex review, 2026-06). hypot() squares sig_dm, so a negative residual
 757         # gives the same |ΔDM| smearing magnitude.
 758         dm_smear = self.dm_init + p.delta_dm
 759         if model_key in {"M1", "M3"}:
 760             sig_full = self._smearing_sigma(dm_smear, p.zeta)
 761         else:
 762             sig_full = self._smearing_sigma(dm_smear, 0.0)
 763 
 764         if freq_subset is None:
 765             sig = sig_full[:, None]
 766         else:
 767             sig = sig_full[freq_subset, None]
 768 
 769         # Guard against non-physical width
 770         sig = np.clip(sig, 1e-6, None)
 771 
 772         if model_key in {"M2", "M3"} and p.tau_1ghz > 1e-6:
 773             alpha = p.alpha
 774             tau = p.tau_1ghz * (freq / 1.0) ** (-alpha)
 775             tau = np.clip(tau, 1e-6, None)[:, None]
 776 
 777             beta_pbf = float(np.clip(p.beta, BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MIN, BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX))
 778             if beta_pbf >= BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX - BETA_EXP_EPS:
 779                 return amp[:, None] * analytic_gaussian_exp_convolution(self.time, mu, sig, tau)
 780             return amp[:, None] * gaussian_powerlaw_convolution(
 781                 self.time, mu, sig, tau, beta_pbf
 782             )
 783 
 784         # Non-scattering models (M0, M1) or negligible tau
 785         gauss = (1.0 / (np.sqrt(2.0 * np.pi) * sig)) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((self.time - mu) / sig) ** 2)
 786         # Normalize
 787         gauss_sum = np.sum(gauss, axis=1, keepdims=True)
 788         safe_gauss_sum = np.clip(gauss_sum, 1e-30, None)
 789 
 790         if model_key not in {"M0", "M1", "M2", "M3"}:
 791             raise ValueError(f"unknown model '{model_key}'")
 792 
 793         return amp[:, None] * (gauss / safe_gauss_sum)

 795     def log_likelihood(self, p: FRBParams, model: str = "M3") -> float:
 796         if self.data is None or self.noise_std is None:
 797             raise RuntimeError("need observed data + noise_std for likelihood")
 798 
 799         # Use pre-calculated validity mask
 800         if self.valid is None or not np.any(self.valid):
 801             return -np.inf
 802 
 803         # Broadcast noise to full shape before masking
 804         ns = self.noise_std
 805         if ns.ndim == 1:
 806             ns = ns[:, None]
 807         noise_std_full = np.broadcast_to(ns, self.data.shape)
 808         noise_valid = noise_std_full[self.valid]
 809         data_valid = self.data[self.valid]
 810 
 811         # Calculate model only for valid channels
 812         model_valid = self(p, model, freq_subset=self.valid)
 813 
 814         resid = (data_valid - model_valid) / noise_valid
 815         return -0.5 * np.sum(resid**2)

 817     def log_likelihood_gain_marginal(self, p: FRBParams, model: str = "M3") -> float:
 818         """Gaussian log-L with a per-channel amplitude (gain) marginalized analytically.
 819 
 820         The model factorizes as g_f * K_f(t): K_f is the UNIT-amplitude scattering
 821         kernel (evaluated with c0=1, gamma=0) carrying the per-channel temporal
 822         shape tau(f), and g_f is a free per-channel gain that absorbs the burst
 823         spectrum AND diffractive scintillation. With a flat prior on g_f, the gain
 824         integral is the matched-filter (F-statistic) marginal likelihood per channel
 825 
 826             ln L_f = -0.5 (S_dd - S_dk^2/S_kk)/sig_f^2 - 0.5 ln(S_kk) + 0.5 ln(2 pi sig_f^2)
 827 
 828         with S_dd=sum_t d^2, S_dk=sum_t d K, S_kk=sum_t K^2 over the on-pulse window.
 829         This whitens AMPLITUDE residuals (scintillation no longer inflates chi2) so
 830         the per-channel chi2 is a valid scattering goodness-of-fit gate; the profiled
 831         g_f (see gain_spectrum) is the scintillation/Delta-nu_d probe. A purely
 832         temporal (shape) misfit -- e.g. a model that cannot reach the burst peak --
 833         is NOT absorbed by g_f and remains visible.
 834         """
 835         if self.data is None or self.noise_std is None:
 836             raise RuntimeError("need observed data + noise_std for likelihood")
 837         if self.valid is None or not np.any(self.valid):
 838             return -np.inf
 839 
 840         K = self(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), model, freq_subset=self.valid)
 841         d = self.data[self.valid]
 842         sig = np.clip(self.noise_std[self.valid], 1e-9, None)
 843         var = sig**2
 844         S_dd = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d, d)
 845         S_dk = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d, K)
 846         S_kk = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", K, K)
 847         ok = S_kk > 1e-30
 848         S_kk_safe = np.where(ok, S_kk, 1.0)
 849         # gain=0 baseline (S_dd/var) where the model has no support in a channel
 850         chi2min = np.where(ok, (S_dd - S_dk**2 / S_kk_safe) / var, S_dd / var)
 851         occam = np.where(ok, -0.5 * np.log(S_kk_safe), 0.0)
 852         const = 0.5 * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * var)
 853         ll = float(np.sum(-0.5 * chi2min + occam + const))
 854         return ll if np.isfinite(ll) else -np.inf
 855

 870     def log_likelihood_gain_marginal_gp(
 871         self,
 872         p: FRBParams,
 873         model: str = "M3",
 874         delta_nu_d_MHz: float | None = None,
 875         mu_degree: int = 1,
 876         sigma_g2: float | None = None,
 877     ) -> float:
 878         """Gain-marginal log-L with a frequency-correlated (scintillation) GP prior.
 879 
 880         Generalizes :meth:`log_likelihood_gain_marginal`: the per-channel gains
 881         g_f are no longer independent with a flat prior but a Gaussian process
 882         whose Lorentzian frequency ACF has half-width ``delta_nu_d_MHz`` (the
 883         diffractive scintillation bandwidth). The temporal matched-filter
 884         statistics are IDENTICAL to the flat path; only the amplitude block
 885         changes (see :func:`_gp_amplitude_logL`).
 886 
 887         Per consensus_logL the per-band marginal is
 888 
 889             logL = -0.5 sum_f chi2min_f                          [temporal, shared with flat]
 890                    + 0.5 sum_f ln(2 pi sig_f^2)                  [data/MF normalization const]
 891                    + logL_amp(ahat, v, nu, delta_nu_d)          [spectral GP block]
 892 
 893         where ahat_f = S_dk,f/S_kk,f, v_f = sig_f^2/S_kk,f and
 894         chi2min_f = (S_dd - S_dk^2/S_kk)/sig_f^2.
 895 
 896         Dispatch / fallback:
 897         * ``delta_nu_d_MHz is None`` -> returns ``log_likelihood_gain_marginal``
 898           VERBATIM (exact flat-prior regression anchor; the GP math is never
 899           duplicated).
 900         * fewer than ``mu_degree + 2`` live, model-supported channels -> same
 901           flat fallback (cannot profile mu + the GP simultaneously).
 902         """
 903         if delta_nu_d_MHz is None:
 904             return self.log_likelihood_gain_marginal(p, model)
 905         if self.data is None or self.noise_std is None:
 906             raise RuntimeError("need observed data + noise_std for likelihood")
 907         if self.valid is None or not np.any(self.valid):
 908             return -np.inf
 909 
 910         # --- temporal matched-filter statistics (identical to the flat path) ---
 911         K = self(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), model, freq_subset=self.valid)
 912         d = self.data[self.valid]
 913         sig = np.clip(self.noise_std[self.valid], 1e-9, None)
 914         var = sig**2
 915         S_dd = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d, d)
 916         S_dk = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d, K)
 917         S_kk = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", K, K)
 918         ok = S_kk > 1e-30  # channels with model support; GP runs on these
 919         n_supported = int(np.count_nonzero(ok))
 920 
 921         # Temporal residual is delta_nu_d-INDEPENDENT and shared with the flat path.
 922         S_kk_safe = np.where(ok, S_kk, 1.0)
 923         chi2min = np.where(ok, (S_dd - S_dk**2 / S_kk_safe) / var, S_dd / var)
 924         temporal = float(np.sum(-0.5 * chi2min))
 925         # data/MF normalization const (matches the flat code's +0.5 ln 2pi sig^2).
 926         const = float(np.sum(0.5 * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * var)))
 927 
 928         if n_supported < int(mu_degree) + 2:
 929             # Cannot profile mu + GP; fall back to the flat marginal (regression-safe).
 930             return self.log_likelihood_gain_marginal(p, model)
 931 
 932         # --- spectral GP block on the supported channels ---
 933         ahat = S_dk[ok] / S_kk[ok]
 934         v = var[ok] / S_kk[ok]
 935         nu_MHz = self.freq[self.valid][ok] * 1.0e3  # GHz -> MHz
 936         try:
 937             logL_amp, _s2, _mu, _m = _gp_amplitude_logL(
 938                 ahat,
 939                 v,
 940                 nu_MHz,
 941                 float(delta_nu_d_MHz),
 942                 mu_degree=int(mu_degree),
 943                 sigma_g2=sigma_g2,
 944             )
 945         except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
 946             return -np.inf
 947 
 948         ll = temporal + const + logL_amp
 949         return ll if np.isfinite(ll) else -np.inf

 951     def scint_gain_summary(
 952         self,
 953         p: FRBParams,
 954         model: str = "M3",
 955         delta_nu_d_MHz: float | None = None,
 956         mu_degree: int = 1,
 957     ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 958         """Recover the GLS smooth mean mu, residual gains, ML sigma_g^2 and the
 959         modulation index at parameters *p* and a given ``delta_nu_d_MHz``.
 960 
 961         Returns a dict over the LIVE+model-supported channels: ``freq_MHz``,
 962         ``ahat`` (matched-filter gain estimates), ``mu`` (smooth GLS envelope),
 963         ``resid`` (ahat - mu, the per-channel scintillation residual),
 964         ``sigma_g2``, ``modulation_index``, ``delta_nu_d_MHz``.
 965         """
 966         if self.data is None or self.noise_std is None:
 967             raise RuntimeError("need observed data + noise_std for likelihood")
 968         K = self(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), model, freq_subset=self.valid)
 969         d = self.data[self.valid]
 970         sig = np.clip(self.noise_std[self.valid], 1e-9, None)
 971         var = sig**2
 972         S_dk = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", d, K)
 973         S_kk = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", K, K)
 974         ok = S_kk > 1e-30
 975         ahat = S_dk[ok] / S_kk[ok]
 976         v = var[ok] / S_kk[ok]
 977         nu_MHz = self.freq[self.valid][ok] * 1.0e3
 978         if delta_nu_d_MHz is None or int(np.count_nonzero(ok)) < int(mu_degree) + 2:
 979             # No GP -> smooth mean is the flat-weighted polynomial, residual=ahat-mu.
 980             span = float(nu_MHz.max() - nu_MHz.min()) if nu_MHz.size else 1.0
 981             nu_c = (nu_MHz - nu_MHz.mean()) / (span if span > 0 else 1.0)
 982             X = np.vander(nu_c, N=int(mu_degree) + 1, increasing=True)
 983             beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, ahat, rcond=None)
 984             mu = X @ beta
 985             return dict(
 986                 freq_MHz=nu_MHz,
 987                 ahat=ahat,
 988                 mu=mu,
 989                 resid=ahat - mu,
 990                 sigma_g2=float("nan"),
 991                 modulation_index=float(
 992                     np.nanstd((ahat - mu) / np.where(np.abs(mu) > 1e-30, mu, np.nan))
 993                 ),
 994                 delta_nu_d_MHz=delta_nu_d_MHz,
 995             )
 996         _ll, s2, mu, mod = _gp_amplitude_logL(
 997             ahat, v, nu_MHz, float(delta_nu_d_MHz), mu_degree=int(mu_degree)
 998         )
 999         return dict(
1000             freq_MHz=nu_MHz,
1001             ahat=ahat,
1002             mu=mu,
1003             resid=ahat - mu,
1004             sigma_g2=s2,
1005             modulation_index=mod,
1006             delta_nu_d_MHz=float(delta_nu_d_MHz),
1007         )

1009     def log_likelihood_student_t(self, p: FRBParams, model: str = "M3", nu: float = 5.0) -> float:
1010         if self.data is None or self.noise_std is None:
1011             raise RuntimeError("need observed data + noise_std for likelihood")
1012         # Use pre-calculated validity mask
1013         if self.valid is None or not np.any(self.valid):
1014             return -np.inf
1015 
1016         # Broadcast noise to full shape before masking
1017         ns = self.noise_std
1018         if ns.ndim == 1:
1019             ns = ns[:, None]
1020         noise_std_full = np.broadcast_to(ns, self.data.shape)
1021         noise_valid = noise_std_full[self.valid]
1022         data_valid = self.data[self.valid]
1023         model_valid = self(p, model, freq_subset=self.valid)
1024 
1025         resid = (data_valid - model_valid) / noise_valid
1026 
1027         # Student-t log-pdf up to constant per element
1028         # logL = sum( - (nu+1)/2 * log(1 + r^2/nu) ) - N * 0.5*log(nu*pi) - sum(log(sigma))
1029         r2_over_nu = (resid**2) / nu
1030         term = -0.5 * (nu + 1.0) * np.log1p(r2_over_nu)
1031 
1032         # Constant term accounts for valid pixels only
1033         n_pix = data_valid.size
1034         const = (
1035             -0.5 * n_pix * np.log(nu * np.pi) - np.sum(np.log(noise_valid)) * data_valid.shape[1]
1036         )
1037 
1038         return const + float(np.sum(term))

1091     def _is_log_param(self, name: str) -> bool:

1095         multi-component variants ('c0_1', 'zeta_2', etc.) consistently.

1103     def _init_walkers(self, p0, key: str, nwalk: int):
1104         names = self._ORDER[key] if key in self._ORDER else self.custom_order[key]
1105         lower, upper = zip(*(self.priors[n] for n in names))
1106         lower = np.array(lower, dtype=float)
1107         upper = np.array(upper, dtype=float)
1108 
1109         centre = []
1110         widths = []
1111         frac = self.walker_width_frac
1112         for i, n in enumerate(names):
1113             if hasattr(p0, n):
1114                 val = getattr(p0, n)
1115             elif isinstance(p0, dict):
1116                 val = p0.get(n, (lower[i] + upper[i]) / 2.0)
1117             else:
1118                 val = (lower[i] + upper[i]) / 2.0
1119 
1120             # Use consistent log-param checking
1121             if self._is_log_param(n):
1122                 lo = max(lower[i], 1e-30)
1123                 hi = max(upper[i], lo * (1.0 + 1e-6))
1124                 centre.append(np.log(max(val, 1e-30)))
1125                 widths.append(frac * (np.log(hi) - np.log(lo)))
1126             else:
1127                 centre.append(val)
1128                 widths.append(frac * (upper[i] - lower[i]))
1129 
1130         centre = np.array(centre)
1131         widths = np.clip(np.array(widths), 1e-6, None)
1132 
1133         walkers = np.random.normal(centre, widths, size=(nwalk, len(names)))
1134 
1135         # Clip in appropriate domain using consistent log-param checking
1136         for j, n in enumerate(names):
1137             if self._is_log_param(n):
1138                 walkers[:, j] = np.clip(
1139                     walkers[:, j],
1140                     np.log(max(lower[j], 1e-30)),
1141                     np.log(max(upper[j], 1e-30)),
1142                 )
1143             else:
1144                 walkers[:, j] = np.clip(walkers[:, j], lower[j], upper[j])
1145 
1146         return walkers

1261     chain = sampler.get_chain(discard=discard)
1262     n_steps, n_walkers, n_params = chain.shape
1263 
1264     if n_steps < 10:
1265         return {"max_rhat": np.inf, "converged": False, "warning": "Too few steps"}
1266 
1267     results = {}
1268     rhats = []

1270     for i in range(n_params):
1271         # For each parameter, compute R̂
1272         # Treat each walker as a separate chain
1273         chains = chain[:, :, i].T  # shape: (n_walkers, n_steps)
1274 
1275         n = chains.shape[1]  # number of samples per chain
1276         m = chains.shape[0]  # number of chains (walkers)
1277 
1278         # Chain means
1279         chain_means = np.mean(chains, axis=1)
1280         # Overall mean
1281         overall_mean = np.mean(chain_means)
1282 
1283         # Between-chain variance
1284         B = n / (m - 1) * np.sum((chain_means - overall_mean) ** 2)
1285 
1286         # Within-chain variance
1287         chain_vars = np.var(chains, axis=1, ddof=1)
1288         W = np.mean(chain_vars)
1289 
1290         # Pooled variance estimate
1291         if W < 1e-30:
1292             # Chains haven't moved - not converged
1293             rhat = np.inf
1294         else:
1295             var_hat = (1 - 1 / n) * W + (1 / n) * B
1296             rhat = np.sqrt(var_hat / W)
1297 
1298         results[f"param_{i}"] = float(rhat)
1299         rhats.append(rhat)

1350             # = sigma_alpha * 4/(alpha-2)^2, else an alpha-space intent lands

1352             # docs/adr/0006 addendum).

1355                 sigma_a * 4.0 / (mu_a - 2.0) ** 2,

1378     abs_min: float = _MIN_POS,  # floor for positive parameters

1380     log_weight_pos: bool = False,  # True → Jeffreys p(x)∝1/x   (still linear sampling)
1381     absolute_bounds: bool = False,  # True → init-independent physical priors (for nested sampling)
1382 ) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[float, float]], bool]:
1383     """
1384     Build simple linear-space top-hat priors that *won’t* strangle the chain.
1385 
1386     Parameters
1387     ----------
1388     init
1389         The optimiser-derived initial parameter set.
1390     scale
1391         Half-width multiplier around each init value.
1392     abs_min
1393         Lower floor for every positive-definite parameter.
1394     abs_max
1395         Optional per-parameter upper caps, e.g. {"tau_1ghz": 1e5}.
1396     log_weight_pos
1397         If True, you still sample in linear units but will later *add*
1398         -log(x) to the log-prior for each positive parameter.
1399     """
1400     pri = {}
1401 
1402     # Map parameters to their specific bounds
1403     # If not in this map, use defaults
1404     param_bounds = {
1405         "c0": (AMP_MIN, AMP_MAX),
1406         "tau_1ghz": (WIDTH_MIN, WIDTH_MAX),
1407         "zeta": (WIDTH_MIN, WIDTH_MAX),
1408         "delta_dm": (
1409             -DM_RESID_MAX,
1410             DM_RESID_MAX,
1411         ),  # residual DM around dm_init (small), not full DM_MAX
1412         "gamma": (-5.0, 5.0),  # Spectral index bounds
1413         "t0": (
1414             init.t0 - 2 * max(init.tau_1ghz, 10.0),
1415             init.t0 + 2 * max(init.tau_1ghz, 10.0),
1416         ),  # Dynamic t0 window
1417         "beta": (BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MIN, BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX),
1418     }
1419 
1420     ceiling = abs_max or {}
1421 
1422     for name, val in asdict(init).items():
1423         # Determine specific bounds for this parameter
1424         if name in param_bounds:
1425             hard_min, hard_max = param_bounds[name]
1426         else:
1427             hard_min, hard_max = abs_min, 1e6
1428 
1429         if absolute_bounds and name != "t0":
1430             # Init-independent physical prior: use the hard bounds directly.
1431             # The init-anchored val ± scale·|val| window collapses to ~0 half-width
1432             # when val ≈ 0 (e.g. gamma=0 → [-0.5, 0.5]), which can exclude the true
1433             # value and trap a global sampler in a wrong mode (observed: a trivial
1434             # init railed M3 to τ→0, ΔlnZ≈320 vs a data-driven init, purely because
1435             # its gamma=0 window excluded the true γ≈-2.6). For evidence-based model
1436             # selection the prior MUST NOT depend on the init at all. t0 is excluded:

1451         pri[name] = (lower, upper)

1463     if f_factor == 1 and t_factor == 1:

1473 def classify_fit_quality(
1474     chi2_reduced: float,
1475     r_squared: float | None = None,
1476     normality_pvalue: float | None = None,
1477 ) -> tuple[str, list]:
1478     """Classify fit quality from chi2_reduced (PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL).
1479 
1480     The reduced chi-squared is the primary, trustworthy gate when the noise is
1481     well estimated: a value near 1 means the model fits to within the noise. The
1482     noise-weighted R^2 is deliberately NOT a gate here -- for faint (low-S/N)
1483     bursts the signal variance is small relative to the noise, so R^2 is low even
1484     for a correct model (a fit at chi2_red ~ 1 can have R^2 well below 0.5).
1485     Treating R^2 < 0.5 as a hard failure (the previous behavior) spuriously
1486     rejected good faint-burst fits. R^2 and the residual-normality p-value are
1487     reported as informational notes only; note that at the ~10^4-pixel sample
1488     sizes here the Shapiro normality p-value is ~0 even for excellent fits.
1489 
1490     Returns (flag, notes) where flag is "PASS", "MARGINAL", or "FAIL".
1491     """
1492     notes: list = []
1493     if chi2_reduced is None or not np.isfinite(chi2_reduced):
1494         return "FAIL", ["Non-finite chi2_red"]
1495 
1496     if chi2_reduced > CHI_SQ_RED_FAIL_MAX:
1497         flag = "FAIL"
1498         notes.append(f"Catastrophic chi2_red ({chi2_reduced:.1f})")
1499     elif chi2_reduced > CHI_SQ_RED_GOOD_MAX:
1500         flag = "MARGINAL"
1501         notes.append(f"Elevated chi2_red ({chi2_reduced:.2f})")
1502     elif chi2_reduced < CHI_SQ_RED_SUSPICIOUSLY_LOW:
1503         flag = "MARGINAL"
1504         notes.append(f"Suspiciously low chi2_red ({chi2_reduced:.2f}); noise may be overestimated")
1505     else:
1506         flag = "PASS"
1507 
1508     # Informational only -- these do NOT change the flag.
1509     if r_squared is not None and np.isfinite(r_squared) and r_squared < R_SQ_MARGINAL_MIN:
1510         notes.append(
1511             f"Low weighted R2 ({r_squared:.3f}) [informational; expected for low-S/N bursts]"
1512         )
1513     if (
1514         normality_pvalue is not None
1515         and np.isfinite(normality_pvalue)
1516         and normality_pvalue < RESIDUAL_NORMALITY_PVALUE
1517     ):
1518         notes.append(f"Non-normal residuals (p={normality_pvalue:.1e}) [informational at large N]")
1519     return flag, notes

1522 def goodness_of_fit(
1523     data: NDArray[np.floating],
1524     model: NDArray[np.floating],
1525     noise_std: NDArray[np.floating],
1526     n_params: int,
1527 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1528     """Compute comprehensive goodness-of-fit metrics and validation flags."""
1529     residual = data - model
1530     # Ensure noise broadcast correctly
1531     noise_std_safe = np.clip(np.atleast_1d(noise_std), 1e-9, None)
1532     if noise_std_safe.ndim == 1 and data.ndim == 2:
1533         noise_std_safe = noise_std_safe[:, np.newaxis]
1534 
1535     # Create valid mask based on noise threshold
1536     valid_mask = noise_std > 1e-9
1537     # Ensure mask broadcasts to data shape if needed
1538     if valid_mask.ndim == 1 and data.ndim == 2:
1539         valid_mask = valid_mask[:, np.newaxis]
1540     valid_mask = np.broadcast_to(valid_mask, data.shape)
1541 
1542     # Use only valid pixels for statistics
1543     resid_valid = residual[valid_mask]
1544     # Broadcast noise_std_safe to data shape before masking
1545     noise_std_full = np.broadcast_to(noise_std_safe, data.shape)
1546     noise_valid = noise_std_full[valid_mask]
1547     data_valid = data[valid_mask]
1548 
1549     n_valid = resid_valid.size
1550 
1551     # 1. Chi-squared
1552     chi2 = np.sum((resid_valid / noise_valid) ** 2)
1553     ndof = n_valid - n_params
1554     chi2_reduced = chi2 / ndof if ndof > 0 else np.inf
1555 
1556     # 2. R-squared
1557     ss_res = np.sum((resid_valid / noise_valid) ** 2)
1558     # Weighted calculation on valid data only
1559     weights = 1.0 / noise_valid**2
1560     mean_data = np.average(data_valid, weights=weights)
1561     ss_tot = np.sum(((data_valid - mean_data) / noise_valid) ** 2)
1562     r_squared = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot) if ss_tot > 0 else -np.inf
1563 
1564     # 3. Normality Test (Shapiro-Wilk)
1565     # SciPy stats.shapiro warns when N > 5000 as the p-value computation becomes
1566     # inaccurate. We calculate a slice step to strictly cap the sample size at 5000.
1567     data_flat = resid_valid.flatten()
1568     step = max(1, int(np.ceil(len(data_flat) / 5000)))
1569     test_resids = data_flat[::step]
1570     try:
1571         _, normality_pvalue = stats.shapiro(test_resids)
1572         normality_pass = normality_pvalue > RESIDUAL_NORMALITY_PVALUE
1573     except Exception:
1574         normality_pvalue = 0.0
1575         normality_pass = False
1576 
1577     # 4. Bias Test
1578     bias_mean = np.mean(resid_valid)
1579     bias_std = np.std(resid_valid)
1580     bias_sem = bias_std / np.sqrt(resid_valid.size)
1581     bias_nsigma = abs(bias_mean) / bias_sem if bias_sem > 0 else 0.0
1582     # bias_pass = bias_nsigma < 3.0
1583 
1584     # 5. Durbin-Watson (Autocorrelation)
1585     # We can compute it on the flattened valid array
1586     diffs = np.diff(data_flat)
1587     dw_stat = np.sum(diffs**2) / np.sum(data_flat**2)
1588     # autocorr_pass = RESIDUAL_AUTOCORR_DW_MIN <= dw_stat <= RESIDUAL_AUTOCORR_DW_MAX
1589 
1590     # 6. Quality Flag -- driven by reduced chi-squared (the trustworthy gate when
1591     # noise is well estimated). R^2 and normality are informational only; see
1592     # classify_fit_quality for why noise-weighted R^2 is not a gate for faint
1593     # bursts.
1594     quality, notes = classify_fit_quality(chi2_reduced, r_squared, normality_pvalue)
1595 
1596     # Autocorrelation of profile
1597     residual_profile = np.sum(residual, axis=0)
1598     residual_profile -= np.mean(residual_profile)
1599     start_autocorr = np.correlate(residual_profile, residual_profile, mode="same")
1600     center_val = start_autocorr[len(start_autocorr) // 2]
1601     norm_autocorr = start_autocorr / center_val if center_val > 0 else start_autocorr
1602 
1603     return {
1604         "chi2": float(chi2),
1605         "chi2_reduced": float(chi2_reduced),
1606         "r_squared": float(r_squared),
1607         "ndof": int(ndof),
1608         "residual_rms": float(np.std(resid_valid)),
1609         "residual_autocorr": norm_autocorr,  # Keep array for plotting
1610         "normality_pvalue": float(normality_pvalue),
1611         "bias_nsigma": float(bias_nsigma),
1612         "durbin_watson": float(dw_stat),
1613         "quality_flag": quality,
1614         "validation_notes": notes,
1615     }

1 #!/usr/bin/env python
   2 """Driver: joint CHIME+DSA scattering fit for one burst.
   3 
   4 Reads the two single-band HPCC run-configs (<b>_chime_run.yaml, <b>_dsa_run.yaml),
   5 rebuilds each band's preprocessed FRBModel + data-driven init exactly as the
   6 single-band pipeline does (same freq-orientation flip, trim, noise estimate),
   7 then runs the shared-(tau,alpha) joint sampler from burstfit_joint.
   8 
   9 Writes <RUNS>/data/joint/<b>_joint_fit.json with the shared alpha / tau_1ghz
  10 posteriors + per-band params, for direct comparison against the single-band
  11 tau_1ghz rails.
  12 
  13   python run_joint_fit.py <burst> [nlive] [nproc]
  14 """
  15 
  16 import argparse
  17 import json
  18 import os
  19 import sys
  20 from pathlib import Path
  21 
  22 REPO = os.environ.get("FABER2026_ANALYSIS", next(str(p) for p in Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / "pyproject.toml").exists()))
  23 RUNS = os.environ.get("FABER2026_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
  24 sys.path.insert(0, REPO)

  30 from scattering.scat_analysis.burstfit_init import data_driven_initial_guess
  31 from scattering.scat_analysis.burstfit_joint import fit_joint_scattering
  32 from scattering.scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
  33 from scattering.scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
  34 from scattering.scat_analysis.pipeline.optimization import refine_initial_guess_mle

  37 def prepare(cfg_path, name, outdir):
  38     """Rebuild a single band's FRBModel + data-driven init from its run-config."""
  39     cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
  40     tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
  41     ds = BurstDataset(
  42         cfg["path"],

  46         f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]),
  47         t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
  48         outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
  49         onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FABER2026_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
  50         onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FABER2026_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")),
  51         onpulse_thresh=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_THRESH", "3.0")),
  52     )
  53     model = ds.model
  54     dm_init = float(cfg.get("dm_init", 0.0))
  55     model.dm_init = dm_init
  56     init = data_driven_initial_guess(
  57         data=model.data,
  58         freq=model.freq,
  59         time=model.time,
  60         dm=dm_init,
  61         verbose=False,
  62     ).params
  63     init = refine_initial_guess_mle(model, init)

  71     ap.add_argument("nproc", nargs="?", type=int, default=8)
  72     # beta is the sampled parameter (ADR-0006); --beta-lo/--beta-hi drive the
  73     # prior directly. The legacy --alpha-lo/--alpha-hi pair is a deprecated
  74     # alias mapped through beta_bounds_from_alpha_bounds inside the library
  75     # (only alpha >= 4 is reachable on the thin-screen branch, so the old
  76     # default (2.0, 6.0) silently truncates to beta in [3, 4]).
  77     ap.add_argument("--beta-lo", dest="beta_lo", type=float, default=None)
  78     ap.add_argument("--beta-hi", dest="beta_hi", type=float, default=None)
  79     ap.add_argument("--alpha-lo", type=float, default=2.0)
  80     ap.add_argument("--alpha-hi", type=float, default=6.0)
  81     ap.add_argument(
  82         "--marginalize-gain",
  83         action="store_true",
  84         help="per-channel gain marginalized (absorbs scintillation); 8-dim fit",
  85     )
  86     ap.add_argument(
  87         "--marginalize-gain-gp",
  88         "--scint",
  89         dest="marginalize_gain_gp",
  90         action="store_true",
  91         help="gain marginalized with a Lorentzian scintillation GP prior; "
  92         "samples Delta_nu_d per band (10-dim fit)",
  93     )
  94     ap.add_argument(
  95         "--mu-degree",
  96         type=int,
  97         default=1,
  98         help="polynomial degree of the smooth GLS spectral envelope (GP path)",
  99     )
 100     ap.add_argument(
 101         "--components-C",
 102         dest="components_C",
 103         type=int,
 104         default=1,
 105         help="number of temporal components (sub-pulses) in the CHIME band",
 106     )
 107     ap.add_argument(
 108         "--components-D",
 109         dest="components_D",
 110         type=int,
 111         default=1,
 112         help="number of temporal components (sub-pulses) in the DSA band",
 113     )
 114     ap.add_argument(

 116         dest="force_multi",
 117         action="store_true",
 118         help="run the multi-component likelihood even at C1D1, so its lnZ "

 123         dest="shared_zeta",
 124         action="store_true",
 125         help="ONE frequency-evolving intrinsic width zeta(nu)=zeta_1ghz*nu^x_zeta "

 144     a = ap.parse_args()

 148     multi = a.components_C > 1 or a.components_D > 1 or a.force_multi
 149 
 150     cfg_dir = f"{RUNS}/configs"
 151     out_dir = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
 152     os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
 153 
 154     cC = f"{cfg_dir}/{a.burst}_chime_run.yaml"
 155     cD = f"{cfg_dir}/{a.burst}_dsa_run.yaml"
 156     for c in (cC, cD):

 158             sys.exit(f"missing config: {c}")

 161     model_C, init_C = prepare(cC, f"{a.burst}_chime", out_dir)
 162     model_D, init_D = prepare(cD, f"{a.burst}_dsa", out_dir)
 163     print(
 164         f"[{a.burst}] CHIME init: tau={init_C.tau_1ghz:.3g} a={init_C.alpha:.2g} | "
 165         f"DSA init: tau={init_D.tau_1ghz:.3g} a={init_D.alpha:.2g}",
 166         flush=True,
 167     )
 168 
 169     res = fit_joint_scattering(
 170         model_C=model_C,
 171         init_C=init_C,
 172         model_D=model_D,
 173         init_D=init_D,
 174         beta_bounds=beta_bounds,
 175         alpha_bounds=None if beta_bounds else (a.alpha_lo, a.alpha_hi),
 176         nlive=a.nlive,
 177         nproc=a.nproc,

 179         marginalize_gain_gp=a.marginalize_gain_gp,

 181         mu_degree=a.mu_degree,
 182         components_C=a.components_C,
 183         components_D=a.components_D,
 184         force_multi=a.force_multi,
 185         gain_s2=a.gain_s2,
 186     )
 187 
 188     pct = res["percentiles"]
 189     names = res["param_names"]
 190 
 191     def med(n):  # median (+err_plus/-err_minus)
 192         d = pct[n]
 193         return d["median"], d["err_minus"], d["err_plus"]
 194 
 195     a_m, a_lo, a_hi = med("alpha")
 196     b_m, b_lo, b_hi = med("beta")
 197     t_m, t_lo, t_hi = med("tau_1ghz")
 198     summary = {
 199         "burst": a.burst,
 200         "marginalize_gain": bool(a.marginalize_gain),
 201         "marginalize_gain_gp": bool(a.marginalize_gain_gp),
 202         "shared_zeta": bool(a.shared_zeta),
 203         # beta first: gate_one's beta-native path keys off "beta" in fit and
 204         # rails against beta_bounds; alpha is the derived report-only value.
 205         "beta": {"median": b_m, "err_minus": b_lo, "err_plus": b_hi},
 206         "beta_bounds": list(res["beta_bounds"]),
 207         "alpha": {"median": a_m, "err_minus": a_lo, "err_plus": a_hi},
 208         "tau_1ghz": {"median": t_m, "err_minus": t_lo, "err_plus": t_hi},
 209         "log_evidence": res["log_evidence"],
 210         "log_evidence_err": res["log_evidence_err"],
 211         "alpha_bounds": list(res["alpha_bounds"]),
 212         "components_C": a.components_C,
 213         "components_D": a.components_D,
 214         "gain_s2": a.gain_s2,
 215         "percentiles": {n: pct[n] for n in names},
 216         "ncall": res["ncall"],
 217     }

 219     # Recover the per-channel gain spectra at the medians (scintillation probe).
 220     gain_C = gain_D = None
 221     scint = {}
 222     if (a.marginalize_gain or a.marginalize_gain_gp or a.shared_zeta) and not multi:
 223         p = {k: v["median"] for k, v in pct.items()}
 224         if a.shared_zeta:
 225             # ONE width law -> per-band zeta is the array zeta_1ghz*nu^x_zeta on
 226             # that band's full channel axis (matches _JointLogLikelihoodGainSharedZeta).
 227             zc = p["zeta_1ghz"] * np.asarray(model_C.freq, float) ** p["x_zeta"]
 228             zd = p["zeta_1ghz"] * np.asarray(model_D.freq, float) ** p["x_zeta"]
 229         else:
 230             zc, zd = p["zeta_C"], p["zeta_D"]
 231         # beta, not alpha: FRBParams is beta-native post-ADR-0006 (alpha is a
 232         # derived property; the alpha= kwarg TypeErrors). beta -> alpha is
 233         # monotone, so the beta median IS the alpha median's preimage.
 234         pC = FRBParams(
 235             c0=1.0,
 236             t0=p["t0_C"],
 237             gamma=0.0,
 238             zeta=zc,
 239             tau_1ghz=t_m,
 240             beta=p["beta"],
 241             delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"],
 242         )
 243         pD = FRBParams(
 244             c0=1.0,
 245             t0=p["t0_D"],
 246             gamma=0.0,
 247             zeta=zd,
 248             tau_1ghz=t_m,
 249             beta=p["beta"],
 250             delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"],
 251         )
 252         gain_C = model_C.gain_spectrum(pC, "M3")
 253         gain_D = model_D.gain_spectrum(pD, "M3")
 254         summary["gain_recovered"] = True
 255 
 256     if a.marginalize_gain_gp:
 257         import numpy as _np
 258 
 259         # Per-band Delta_nu_d posterior medians + channel width + unresolved flag
 260         # + modulation-index sub-resolution estimate (from the GLS residual gains).
 261         def _chan_w_MHz(freq_GHz):
 262             return float(_np.median(_np.abs(_np.diff(_np.asarray(freq_GHz))))) * 1e3
 263 
 264         dnu_C = med("Delta_nu_d_C")
 265         dnu_D = med("Delta_nu_d_D")
 266         cw_C, cw_D = _chan_w_MHz(model_C.freq), _chan_w_MHz(model_D.freq)
 267         sumC = model_C.scint_gain_summary(pC, "M3", delta_nu_d_MHz=dnu_C[0], mu_degree=a.mu_degree)
 268         sumD = model_D.scint_gain_summary(pD, "M3", delta_nu_d_MHz=dnu_D[0], mu_degree=a.mu_degree)
 269         scint = {
 270             "Delta_nu_d_C": {
 271                 "median": dnu_C[0],
 272                 "err_minus": dnu_C[1],
 273                 "err_plus": dnu_C[2],
 274                 "chan_width_MHz": cw_C,
 275                 "unresolved": bool(dnu_C[0] < cw_C),
 276                 "modulation_index": sumC["modulation_index"],
 277                 "modindex_dnu_d_MHz": float(sumC["modulation_index"] ** 2 * cw_C),
 278                 "sigma_g2": sumC["sigma_g2"],
 279             },
 280             "Delta_nu_d_D": {
 281                 "median": dnu_D[0],
 282                 "err_minus": dnu_D[1],
 283                 "err_plus": dnu_D[2],
 284                 "chan_width_MHz": cw_D,
 285                 "unresolved": bool(dnu_D[0] < cw_D),
 286                 "modulation_index": sumD["modulation_index"],
 287                 "modindex_dnu_d_MHz": float(sumD["modulation_index"] ** 2 * cw_D),
 288                 "sigma_g2": sumD["sigma_g2"],
 289             },
 290         }
 291         summary["scint"] = scint
 292 
 293     if multi:
 294         tag = f"_C{a.components_C}D{a.components_D}"
 295     elif a.shared_zeta:
 296         tag = "_sharedzeta"  # keep the per-band baseline json/npz for comparison
 297     else:
 298         tag = ""
 299     if a.gain_s2 is not None:  # fixed-s2 ladder: never clobber the profiled run
 300         tag += f"_s2-{a.gain_s2:g}"
 301     # No _pbf-* tag: beta drives the PBF family (ADR-0006), so beta-campaign
 302     # outputs are suffix-free and cannot collide with the legacy alpha-era
 303     # *_pbf-exp-exp.json artifacts.
 304     out = f"{out_dir}/{a.burst}_joint_fit{tag}.json"
 305     json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=2)
 306 
 307     # Persist the full weighted posterior + recovered gains + per-band freq axes so

 309     # built without re-running the sampler.
 310     npz = dict(
 311         samples=res["samples"],
 312         weights=res["weights"],
 313         param_names=np.array(names, dtype=object),
 314         alpha_bounds=np.array(res["alpha_bounds"], dtype=float),
 315         freq_C=model_C.freq,
 316         freq_D=model_D.freq,
 317     )
 318     if gain_C is not None:
 319         npz["gain_C"] = gain_C
 320         npz["gain_D"] = gain_D
 321     if a.marginalize_gain_gp:
 322         # Posterior Delta_nu_d columns (so scint_acf.py can cross-check the fit's
 323         # Delta_nu_d against its own ACF estimate) + GLS mean/residual per band.
 324         ci = list(names).index("Delta_nu_d_C")
 325         di = list(names).index("Delta_nu_d_D")
 326         npz["Delta_nu_d_C_samples"] = res["samples"][:, ci]
 327         npz["Delta_nu_d_D_samples"] = res["samples"][:, di]
 328         npz["scint_freq_C_MHz"] = sumC["freq_MHz"]
 329         npz["scint_ahat_C"] = sumC["ahat"]
 330         npz["scint_mu_C"] = sumC["mu"]
 331         npz["scint_freq_D_MHz"] = sumD["freq_MHz"]
 332         npz["scint_ahat_D"] = sumD["ahat"]
 333         npz["scint_mu_D"] = sumD["mu"]
 334     np.savez_compressed(f"{out_dir}/{a.burst}_joint_samples{tag}.npz", **npz)
 335 
 336     # Rail check on the SAMPLED parameter: ADR-0004 flags a median within ~3
 337     # sigma of either beta prior bound (a beta=4 rail is the exponential limit
 338     # / alpha=4-as-limit case and the ADR-0007 re-open trigger).
 339     bb_lo, bb_hi = res["beta_bounds"]
 340     edge = (
 341         " [BETA AT PRIOR EDGE]" if (b_m - 3.0 * b_lo <= bb_lo or b_m + 3.0 * b_hi >= bb_hi) else ""
 342     )
 343     print(
 344         f"\n[{a.burst}] JOINT  beta = {b_m:.3f} (+{b_hi:.3f}/-{b_lo:.3f}){edge}"
 345         f"   alpha = {a_m:.2f} (+{a_hi:.2f}/-{a_lo:.2f})"
 346         f"   tau_1GHz = {t_m:.3g} (+{t_hi:.2g}/-{t_lo:.2g}) ms"
 347         f"   lnZ = {res['log_evidence']:.1f}",
 348         flush=True,
 349     )
 350     if a.marginalize_gain_gp:
 351         for b, s in scint.items():
 352             flag = "UNRESOLVED (upper limit)" if s["unresolved"] else "RESOLVED"
 353             print(
 354                 f"[{a.burst}] {b} = {s['median']:.3g} MHz "
 355                 f"(chan {s['chan_width_MHz']:.3g} MHz) [{flag}]  "
 356                 f"m={s['modulation_index']:.3g} -> dnu_d~{s['modindex_dnu_d_MHz']:.3g} MHz",
 357                 flush=True,
 358             )
 359     print(f"[{a.burst}] wrote {out}", flush=True)
 360 
 361 
 362 if __name__ == "__main__":
 363     main()

1 """
   2 priors_physical.py
   3 ==================
   4 
   5 Astrophysically informed priors for scattering analysis using Galactic
   6 electron density models (NE2001, YMW16).
   7 
   8 This module provides functions to build prior distributions that incorporate
   9 our physical understanding of interstellar scattering:
  10 
  11 1. **Scattering timescale (τ)**: Log-normal prior centered on NE2001 prediction
  12    with ~0.5 dex uncertainty (factor of 3)
  13 
  14 2. **Spectral index (α)**: Gaussian prior centered on theoretical values
  15    - α = 4.0 for thin screen (Gaussian spectrum)
  16    - α = 4.4 for Kolmogorov turbulence
  17 
  18 3. **Intrinsic width (ζ)**: Prior from typical FRB durations
  19 
  20 Usage
  21 -----
  22 ```python
  23 from priors_physical import build_physical_priors, get_ne2001_scattering
  24 
  25 # Get NE2001 prediction
  26 tau_pred, nu_scint = get_ne2001_scattering(ra=180.0, dec=45.0, dm=500.0)
  27 
  28 # Build priors for fitting
  29 priors = build_physical_priors(
  30     ra_deg=180.0,
  31     dec_deg=45.0,
  32     dm=500.0,
  33     freq_ghz=1.0,
  34 )
  35 
  36 # Use with FRBFitter
  37 fitter = FRBFitter(model, priors["bounds"], tau_prior=priors["tau"])
  38 ```
  39 
  40 References
  41 ----------
  42 - NE2001: Cordes & Lazio (2002), astro-ph/0207156
  43 - YMW16: Yao, Manchester & Wang (2017), ApJ 835:29
  44 - Kolmogorov α=4.4: Rickett (1990), ARA&A 28:561
  45 """
  46 
  47 from __future__ import annotations
  48 
  49 import logging
  50 from dataclasses import dataclass
  51 from typing import Dict, Tuple
  52 
  53 import numpy as np
  54 
  55 log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  56 
  57 __all__ = [
  58     "get_ne2001_scattering",
  59     "build_physical_priors",
  60     "PhysicalPriors",
  61     "get_burst_priors_from_catalog",
  62     "TURBULENCE_INDICES",
  63     "log_prob_lognormal",
  64 ]
  65 
  66 # Theoretical spectral indices for different turbulence spectra
  67 TURBULENCE_INDICES = {
  68     "kolmogorov": 4.4,       # β = 11/3, α = 2β/(β-2) ≈ 4.4
  69     "thin_screen": 4.0,      # Gaussian angular spectrum
  70     "square_law": 4.0,       # Structure function ∝ r²
  71     "thick_medium": 3.5,     # Extended scattering region
  72 }
  73 
  74 
  75 @dataclass
  76 class PhysicalPriors:
  77     """Container for physical prior specifications.
  78 
  79     Attributes
  80     ----------
  81     tau_lognormal : tuple
  82         (mu, sigma) for log-normal prior on τ (in log10 space: τ ~ 10^N(μ,σ²))
  83     alpha_gaussian : tuple
  84         (mu, sigma) for Gaussian prior on α
  85     bounds : dict
  86         Parameter bounds for uniform components of priors
  87     ne2001_tau_1ghz : float
  88         NE2001 prediction for τ at 1 GHz (ms)
  89     ne2001_nu_scint : float
  90         NE2001 prediction for scintillation bandwidth (MHz)
  91     """
  92     tau_lognormal: Tuple[float, float]
  93     alpha_gaussian: Tuple[float, float]
  94     bounds: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]]
  95     ne2001_tau_1ghz: float
  96     ne2001_nu_scint: float
  97 
  98     def __repr__(self) -> str:
  99         return (
 100             f"PhysicalPriors(\n"
 101             f"  τ ~ LogNormal(μ={self.tau_lognormal[0]:.2f}, σ={self.tau_lognormal[1]:.2f}) [log10]\n"
 102             f"  α ~ Normal(μ={self.alpha_gaussian[0]:.2f}, σ={self.alpha_gaussian[1]:.2f})\n"
 103             f"  NE2001 prediction: τ(1GHz) = {self.ne2001_tau_1ghz:.3f} ms\n"
 104             f")"
 105         )
 106 
 107 
 108 def get_ne2001_scattering(
 109     ra_deg: float,
 110     dec_deg: float,
 111     dm: float,
 112     freq_mhz: float = 1000.0,
 113     alpha: float = 4.0,
 114 ) -> Tuple[float, float]:
 115     """Query NE2001 for expected scattering at a sky position.
 116 
 117     Parameters
 118     ----------
 119     ra_deg : float
 120         Right ascension in degrees
 121     dec_deg : float
 122         Declination in degrees
 123     dm : float
 124         Dispersion measure (pc cm⁻³)
 125     freq_mhz : float
 126         Frequency in MHz (default 1000 = 1 GHz)
 127     alpha : float
 128         Frequency scaling index (default 4.0)
 129 
 130     Returns
 131     -------
 132     tau_ms : float
 133         Scattering timescale at freq_mhz (ms)
 134     nu_scint_khz : float
 135         Scintillation bandwidth at freq_mhz (kHz)
 136 
 137     Notes
 138     -----
 139     Requires the `mwprop` package: pip install mwprop
 140     Falls back to empirical relation if NE2001 unavailable.
 141     """
 142     try:
 143         from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord
 144         import astropy.units as u
 145         from mwprop.ne2001p.NE2001 import ne2001
 146 
 147         # Convert to Galactic coordinates
 148         coord = SkyCoord(ra=ra_deg*u.deg, dec=dec_deg*u.deg, frame='icrs')
 149         l_deg = coord.galactic.l.deg
 150         b_deg = coord.galactic.b.deg
 151 
 152         # Query NE2001 (ndir=-1 means use DM to infer distance)
 153         Dk, Dv, Du, Dd = ne2001(
 154             ldeg=l_deg,
 155             bdeg=b_deg,
 156             dmd=dm,
 157             ndir=-1,
 158             classic=False,
 159             dmd_only=False,
 160         )
 161 
 162         # τ at 1 GHz from NE2001
 163         tau_1ghz_ms = Dv['TAU']  # Already in ms at 1 GHz
 164 
 165         # Scale to requested frequency
 166         tau_ms = tau_1ghz_ms * (1000.0 / freq_mhz) ** alpha
 167 
 168         # Scintillation bandwidth: Δν = 1/(2πτ)
 169         nu_scint_khz = 1.0 / (2 * np.pi * tau_ms * 1e-3) / 1e3
 170 
 171         return tau_ms, nu_scint_khz
 172 
 173     except ImportError:
 174         log.warning(
 175             "mwprop not available; using empirical DM-τ relation. "
 176             "Install with: pip install mwprop"
 177         )
 178         return _empirical_dm_tau_relation(dm, freq_mhz, alpha)
 179     except Exception as e:
 180         log.warning(f"NE2001 query failed: {e}. Using empirical relation.")
 181         return _empirical_dm_tau_relation(dm, freq_mhz, alpha)
 182

 184 def _empirical_dm_tau_relation(
 185     dm: float,
 186     freq_mhz: float = 1000.0,
 187     alpha: float = 4.0,
 188 ) -> Tuple[float, float]:
 189     """Empirical DM-τ relation from Bhat et al. (2004).
 190 
 191     log₁₀(τ/ms) = -6.46 + 1.07 log₁₀(DM) - 3.86 log₁₀(ν/GHz)
 192 
 193     Valid for pulsars; FRBs may have additional host/IGM contribution.
 194     """
 195     # Bhat (2004) relation at 1 GHz
 196     log_tau = -6.46 + 1.07 * np.log10(dm)
 197     tau_1ghz_ms = 10 ** log_tau
 198 
 199     # Scale to frequency
 200     tau_ms = tau_1ghz_ms * (1000.0 / freq_mhz) ** alpha
 201 
 202     # Scintillation bandwidth
 203     nu_scint_khz = 1.0 / (2 * np.pi * tau_ms * 1e-3) / 1e3
 204 
 205     return tau_ms, nu_scint_khz
 206 
 207 
 208 def build_physical_priors(
 209     ra_deg: float,
 210     dec_deg: float,
 211     dm: float,
 212     freq_ghz: float = 1.0,
 213     tau_uncertainty_dex: float = 0.5,
 214     alpha_mean: float = 4.0,
 215     alpha_std: float = 0.5,
 216     turbulence_model: str = "thin_screen",
 217     allow_host_scattering: bool = True,
 218 ) -> PhysicalPriors:
 219     """Build astrophysically motivated priors for scattering parameters.
 220 
 221     Parameters
 222     ----------
 223     ra_deg : float
 224         Right ascension in degrees
 225     dec_deg : float
 226         Declination in degrees
 227     dm : float
 228         Dispersion measure (pc cm⁻³)
 229     freq_ghz : float
 230         Reference frequency in GHz
 231     tau_uncertainty_dex : float
 232         Uncertainty on τ in dex (0.5 = factor of 3)
 233     alpha_mean : float
 234         Mean of Gaussian prior on α
 235     alpha_std : float
 236         Standard deviation of Gaussian prior on α
 237     turbulence_model : str
 238         Override alpha_mean with theoretical value:
 239         "kolmogorov", "thin_screen", "thick_medium", or None
 240     allow_host_scattering : bool
 241         If True, allow τ to exceed NE2001 prediction (host contribution)
 242 
 243     Returns
 244     -------
 245     PhysicalPriors
 246         Prior specifications for use with FRBFitter
 247     """
 248     # Get NE2001 prediction
 249     freq_mhz = freq_ghz * 1000.0
 250     tau_pred_ms, nu_scint_khz = get_ne2001_scattering(ra_deg, dec_deg, dm, freq_mhz)
 251 
 252     # Scale τ to 1 GHz for consistency with fitting
 253     tau_1ghz_pred = tau_pred_ms * (freq_mhz / 1000.0) ** alpha_mean
 254 
 255     # Log-normal prior on τ: centered on NE2001 prediction
 256     # In log10 space: τ ~ 10^N(log10(τ_pred), σ²)
 257     log10_tau_mean = np.log10(max(tau_1ghz_pred, 1e-6))  # Guard against zero
 258     log10_tau_std = tau_uncertainty_dex
 259 
 260     # Allow host/extragalactic contribution by widening upper bound
 261     if allow_host_scattering:
 262         log10_tau_std = max(log10_tau_std, 1.0)  # At least 1 dex to allow host
 263 
 264     tau_lognormal = (log10_tau_mean, log10_tau_std)
 265 
 266     # Alpha prior
 267     if turbulence_model is not None and turbulence_model in TURBULENCE_INDICES:
 268         alpha_mean = TURBULENCE_INDICES[turbulence_model]
 269 
 270     alpha_gaussian = (alpha_mean, alpha_std)
 271 
 272     # Parameter bounds (uniform components)
 273     # These should be wide enough to not truncate the physical priors
 274     tau_lo = 10 ** (log10_tau_mean - 3 * log10_tau_std)
 275     tau_hi = 10 ** (log10_tau_mean + 3 * log10_tau_std)
 276 
 277     bounds = {
 278         "c0": (0.01, 100.0),
 279         "t0": (-10.0, 50.0),  # ms, relative to data start
 280         "gamma": (-5.0, 5.0),  # spectral index
 281         "zeta": (0.001, 10.0),  # ms, intrinsic width
 282         "tau_1ghz": (max(1e-6, tau_lo), max(100.0, tau_hi)),  # ms
 283         "alpha": (max(2.0, alpha_mean - 3*alpha_std),
 284                   min(6.0, alpha_mean + 3*alpha_std)),
 285         "delta_dm": (-5.0, 5.0),  # pc cm⁻³
 286     }
 287 
 288     log.info(
 289         f"Built physical priors:\n"
 290         f"  Position: ({ra_deg:.2f}, {dec_deg:.2f}) deg\n"
 291         f"  DM: {dm:.1f} pc/cm³\n"
 292         f"  NE2001 τ(1GHz): {tau_1ghz_pred:.4f} ms\n"
 293         f"  τ prior: log10(τ) ~ N({log10_tau_mean:.2f}, {log10_tau_std:.2f}²)\n"
 294         f"  α prior: N({alpha_mean:.2f}, {alpha_std:.2f}²)"
 295     )
 296 
 297     return PhysicalPriors(
 298         tau_lognormal=tau_lognormal,
 299         alpha_gaussian=alpha_gaussian,
 300         bounds=bounds,
 301         ne2001_tau_1ghz=tau_1ghz_pred,
 302         ne2001_nu_scint=nu_scint_khz,
 303     )
 304

 312     Modifies the fitter in-place to use NE2001-informed priors.

 314     # Update alpha prior

 369 # Utility: log-normal prior probability
 370 def log_prob_lognormal(x: float, mu: float, sigma: float) -> float:
 371     """Log probability for log-normal prior (in log10 space).
 372 
 373     x ~ 10^N(μ, σ²) → log10(x) ~ N(μ, σ²)
 374 
 375     Parameters
 376     ----------
 377     x : float
 378         Parameter value (must be positive)
 379     mu : float
 380         Mean of log10(x)
 381     sigma : float
 382         Standard deviation of log10(x)
 383 
 384     Returns
 385     -------
 386     log_prob : float
 387         Log probability density
 388     """
 389     if x <= 0:
 390         return -np.inf
 391 
 392     log10_x = np.log10(x)
 393     # Convert user-facing mode parameterization to the equivalent Normal mean.
 394     # If y = log10(x) ~ Normal(mean, sigma), then the mode of x occurs at:
 395     # y_mode = mean - sigma^2 * ln(10)
 396     # Therefore if mu is provided as y_mode, mean = mu + sigma^2 * ln(10).
 397     log10_mean = mu + (sigma**2) * np.log(10)
 398     z = (log10_x - log10_mean) / sigma
 399 
 400     # Normal PDF for log10(x), plus Jacobian 1/(x * ln(10))
 401     return -0.5 * z**2 - np.log(sigma) - np.log(x) - np.log(np.log(10))

1 """Turbulence-spectrum helpers for the beta-coherent scattering model.
   2 
   3 The fundamental parameter is the electron-density fluctuation spectral index beta
   4 (P_n(q) propto q^{-beta}). For a thin screen with 2 < beta <= 4, both the
   5 pulse-broadening function shape and the frequency-scaling index follow from beta:
   6 
   7     alpha = 2*beta / (beta - 2)          (tau propto nu^{-alpha})
   8     PBF tail ~ t^{-beta/2}  (via gaussian_powerlaw_convolution)
   9 
  10 At beta -> 4 the power-law PBF reduces to the thin-screen exponential (alpha = 4).
  11 The converse also holds and matters for fit design: an exponential PBF (an EMG
  12 burst model) is uniquely the beta = 4 member of this family, so adopting it
  13 commits the fit to alpha = 4 by definition — see the rationale addendum in
  14 docs/adr/0006-beta-coherent-scattering-comodel.md.
  15 """
  16 
  17 from __future__ import annotations
  18 
  19 import numpy as np
  20 
  21 __all__ = [
  22     "KOLMOGOROV_BETA",
  23     "BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MIN",
  24     "BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX",
  25     "BETA_EXP_EPS",
  26     "alpha_from_beta",
  27     "beta_from_alpha_thin_screen",
  28     "beta_bounds_from_alpha_bounds",
  29     "default_joint_beta_bounds",
  30 ]
  31 
  32 KOLMOGOROV_BETA = 11.0 / 3.0
  33 BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MIN = 2.01
  34 BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX = 4.0
  35 # Use the closed-form exponential PBF when beta is within this of 4.
  36 BETA_EXP_EPS = 0.02
  37 
  38 
  39 def alpha_from_beta(beta: float) -> float:
  40     """Frequency-scaling index alpha from turbulence spectral index beta (thin screen, beta <= 4)."""
  41     beta = float(beta)
  42     if beta >= BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX - BETA_EXP_EPS:
  43         return 4.0
  44     if beta <= 2.0:
  45         raise ValueError(f"beta must be > 2 for thin-screen alpha mapping, got {beta}")
  46     return 2.0 * beta / (beta - 2.0)
  47 
  48 
  49 def beta_from_alpha_thin_screen(alpha: float) -> float:
  50     """Inverse of alpha_from_beta for alpha >= 4 (thin-screen branch)."""
  51     alpha = float(alpha)
  52     if alpha <= 2.0:
  53         raise ValueError(f"alpha must be > 2 for thin-screen beta mapping, got {alpha}")
  54     if np.isclose(alpha, 4.0):
  55         return BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX
  56     return 2.0 * alpha / (alpha - 2.0)
  57 
  58 
  59 def beta_bounds_from_alpha_bounds(
  60     alpha_bounds: tuple[float, float],
  61 ) -> tuple[float, float]:
  62     """Map legacy alpha prior bounds to beta bounds on the thin-screen branch.
  63 
  64     Only alpha >= 4 is reachable with beta in (2, 4]; sub-Kolmogorov alpha < 4
  65     requires beta > 4 (extended-medium physics) and is not mapped here.
  66     """
  67     lo_a, hi_a = float(alpha_bounds[0]), float(alpha_bounds[1])
  68     if lo_a == hi_a:
  69         # Degenerate window = fixed alpha. alpha >= 4 pins the corresponding
  70         # beta; alpha < 4 is unreachable on this branch and pins the
  71         # exponential limit beta = 4 (an exponential PBF is uniquely the
  72         # beta = 4 member, so fixed-alpha=4/EMG requests must NOT silently
  73         # widen to the full range -- docs/adr/0006 rationale addendum).
  74         b = beta_from_alpha_thin_screen(lo_a) if lo_a >= 4.0 else BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX
  75         return (b, b)
  76     # Higher alpha -> lower beta; clamp to the integrable PBF regime.
  77     beta_lo = beta_from_alpha_thin_screen(max(hi_a, 4.0 + 1e-6))
  78     beta_hi = beta_from_alpha_thin_screen(max(lo_a, 4.0))
  79     beta_lo = max(beta_lo, BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MIN)
  80     beta_hi = min(beta_hi, BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX)
  81     if beta_lo >= beta_hi:
  82         beta_lo = BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MIN
  83         beta_hi = BETA_THIN_SCREEN_MAX
  84     return (beta_lo, beta_hi)
  85 
  86 
  87 def default_joint_beta_bounds() -> tuple[float, float]:
  88     """Default joint-fit beta bounds (~ alpha in [4, 6] on the thin-screen branch)."""
  89     return beta_bounds_from_alpha_bounds((4.0, 6.0))

   1 """
   2 config_utils.py
   3 ===============
   4 
   5 Utility for reading telescope-specific raw-data parameters from
   6 *telescopes.yaml*.  Keeping this separate avoids a hard dependency on
   7 `pyyaml` in the core physics modules.
   8 """
   9 
  10 from __future__ import annotations
  11 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  12 from pathlib import Path
  13 from typing import Any, Dict, Optional, Union
  14 import os

  20 def resolve_path(path: Union[str, Path], base_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> Path:
  21     """Resolve a path, supporting relative paths and environment variables.
  22 
  23     Parameters
  24     ----------
  25     path : str or Path
  26         The path to resolve. Can be:
  27         - Absolute path: returned as-is
  28         - Relative path: resolved relative to base_dir or CWD
  29         - Contains $VAR or ${VAR}: environment variables are expanded
  30         - Starts with ~: user home directory is expanded
  31     base_dir : Path, optional
  32         Base directory for resolving relative paths. If None, uses current
  33         working directory.
  34 
  35     Returns
  36     -------
  37     Path
  38         The resolved, absolute path.
  39 
  40     Examples
  41     --------
  42     >>> resolve_path("data/burst.npy", base_dir=Path("/project/configs"))
  43     PosixPath('/project/data/burst.npy')
  44     >>> resolve_path("$HOME/data/burst.npy")
  45     PosixPath('/home/user/data/burst.npy')
  46     """
  47     # Convert to string for expansion
  48     path_str = str(path)
  49 
  50     # Expand environment variables (handles both $VAR and ${VAR})
  51     path_str = os.path.expandvars(path_str)
  52 
  53     # Expand user home directory (~)
  54     path_str = os.path.expanduser(path_str)
  55 
  56     # Convert to Path
  57     resolved = Path(path_str)
  58 
  59     # If already absolute, return as-is
  60     if resolved.is_absolute():
  61         return resolved
  62 
  63     # Resolve relative to base_dir or CWD
  64     if base_dir is not None:
  65         resolved = base_dir / resolved
  66     else:
  67         resolved = Path.cwd() / resolved
  68 
  69     # Normalize the path (resolve .. and . components)
  70     return resolved.resolve()
  71

 224 def load_config(path: str | Path, workspace_root: Optional[Path] = None) -> Config:
 225     """Load the full analysis configuration from ``path``.
 226 
 227     The file specified by *path* is expected to contain run-specific options
 228     such as the data ``path``, ``dm_init`` and ``telescope`` choice.  The
 229     corresponding ``telescopes.yaml`` and ``sampler.yaml`` files are assumed to
 230     live in the same directory unless explicit ``telcfg_path`` or
 231     ``sampcfg_path`` entries are provided.
 232 
 233     Parameters
 234     ----------
 235     path : str or Path
 236         Path to the run configuration YAML file.
 237     workspace_root : Path, optional
 238         Root directory of the workspace/project. Used for resolving relative
 239         data paths. If None, defaults to the parent of the config file's directory.
 240 
 241     Notes
 242     -----
 243     Relative paths in the config are resolved in the following order:
 244     1. Relative to config file directory (for telcfg_path, sampcfg_path)
 245     2. Relative to workspace_root (for data paths)
 246 
 247     Environment variables ($VAR) and home directory (~) are expanded in all paths.
 248     """
 249 
 250     run_path = Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
 251     with run_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
 252         cfg = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
 253 
 254     config_dir = run_path.parent
 255 
 256     # Workspace root defaults to grandparent of config (e.g., configs/bursts/x.yaml -> workspace)
 257     if workspace_root is None:
 258         # Try to find workspace root by looking for common markers
 259         workspace_root = config_dir
 260         for _ in range(5):  # Look up to 5 levels
 261             if (workspace_root / "pyproject.toml").exists() or \
 262                (workspace_root / "setup.py").exists() or \
 263                (workspace_root / ".git").exists():
 264                 break
 265             if workspace_root.parent == workspace_root:
 266                 break
 267             workspace_root = workspace_root.parent
 268 
 269     # Resolve telescope and sampler config paths relative to config directory
 270     telcfg_raw = cfg.get("telcfg_path", "telescopes.yaml")

1 """
   2 burstfit_nested.py
   3 ==================
   4 
   5 Nested sampling implementation for rigorous Bayesian model comparison.
   6 
   7 Uses dynesty to compute the Bayesian evidence (marginal likelihood) for each
   8 model in the FRB dynamic spectrum model family (M0-M3). This enables
   9 model comparison via Bayes factors instead of BIC.
  10 
  11 Key advantages over BIC:
  12 - Rigorous marginalization over parameter space
  13 - No asymptotic approximations
  14 - Proper handling of prior volume
  15 - Uncertainty estimates on evidence
  16 
  17 Usage
  18 -----
  19 ```python
  20 from burstfit_nested import fit_models_evidence
  21 
  22 best_model, results = fit_models_evidence(
  23     model=frb_model,
  24     init=initial_params,
  25     model_keys=["M0", "M1", "M2", "M3"],
  26 )
  27 
  28 # Bayes factor between M3 and M2
  29 ln_bf = results["M3"]["log_evidence"] - results["M2"]["log_evidence"]
  30 print(f"ln(BF) = {ln_bf:.1f}")  # >5 is strong evidence for M3
  31 ```
  32 
  33 Bayes Factor Interpretation (Jeffreys' scale):
  34 - |ln(BF)| < 1: Inconclusive
  35 - 1 < |ln(BF)| < 2.5: Weak
  36 - 2.5 < |ln(BF)| < 5: Moderate
  37 - |ln(BF)| > 5: Strong
  38 """
  39 
  40 from __future__ import annotations
  41 
  42 import logging
  43 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  44 from itertools import combinations
  45 from typing import Dict, Optional, Sequence, Tuple, Any
  46 
  47 import numpy as np
  48 from numpy.typing import NDArray
  49 
  50 from .burstfit import FRBModel, FRBParams, build_priors
  51 from .turbulence import beta_from_alpha_thin_screen
  52 
  53 log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  54 
  55 __all__ = [
  56     "fit_models_evidence",
  57     "fit_single_model_nested",
  58     "quick_evidence_comparison",
  59     "NestedSamplingResult",
  60     "interpret_bayes_factor",
  61 ]
  62 
  63 # Model parameter definitions
  64 _PARAM_KEYS = {
  65     "M0": ("c0", "t0", "gamma"),
  66     "M1": ("c0", "t0", "gamma", "zeta"),
  67     "M2": ("c0", "t0", "gamma", "tau_1ghz"),
  68     "M3": ("c0", "t0", "gamma", "zeta", "tau_1ghz", "beta", "delta_dm"),
  69 }
  70 
  71 
  72 @dataclass
  73 class NestedSamplingResult:
  74     """Container for nested sampling results."""
  75 
  76     log_evidence: float
  77     log_evidence_err: float
  78     samples: NDArray[np.floating]
  79     weights: NDArray[np.floating]
  80     param_names: Tuple[str, ...]
  81     model_key: str
  82     nlive: int
  83     ncall: int
  84 
  85     # Derived quantities
  86     percentiles: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
  87     fixed_params: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
  88 
  89     def __post_init__(self):
  90         """Compute parameter percentiles from weighted samples."""
  91         if len(self.percentiles) == 0:
  92             self._compute_percentiles()
  93 
  94     def _compute_percentiles(self):
  95         """Compute median and 68% CI for each parameter."""
  96         for i, name in enumerate(self.param_names):
  97             samples = self.samples[:, i]
  98             # Weighted percentiles
  99             sorted_idx = np.argsort(samples)
 100             sorted_samples = samples[sorted_idx]
 101             sorted_weights = self.weights[sorted_idx]
 102             cumsum = np.cumsum(sorted_weights)
 103             cumsum /= cumsum[-1]
 104 
 105             p16 = sorted_samples[np.searchsorted(cumsum, 0.16)]
 106             p50 = sorted_samples[np.searchsorted(cumsum, 0.50)]
 107             p84 = sorted_samples[np.searchsorted(cumsum, 0.84)]
 108 
 109             self.percentiles[name] = {
 110                 "median": p50,
 111                 "lower": p16,
 112                 "upper": p84,
 113                 "err_minus": p50 - p16,
 114                 "err_plus": p84 - p50,
 115             }
 116 
 117     def get_best_params(self) -> FRBParams:
 118         """Return FRBParams at posterior median."""
 119         full_names = _PARAM_KEYS[self.model_key]
 120         theta = []
 121         for name in full_names:
 122             if name in self.fixed_params:
 123                 theta.append(self.fixed_params[name])
 124             elif name in self.percentiles:
 125                 theta.append(self.percentiles[name]["median"])
 126             else:
 127                 # Should not happen if logic is correct
 128                 theta.append(0.0)
 129         return FRBParams.from_sequence(theta, self.model_key)
 130 
 131     def __repr__(self) -> str:
 132         return (
 133             f"NestedSamplingResult(\n"
 134             f"  model={self.model_key}\n"
 135             f"  log_evidence={self.log_evidence:.2f} ± {self.log_evidence_err:.2f}\n"
 136             f"  nlive={self.nlive}, ncall={self.ncall}\n"
 137             f")"
 138         )
 139 
 140 
 141 def interpret_bayes_factor(ln_bf: float, model1: str = "first model", model2: str = "second model") -> str:
 142     """Interpret log Bayes factor on Jeffreys' scale.
 143 
 144     Parameters
 145     ----------
 146     ln_bf : float
 147         Natural log of Bayes factor = ln(Z_1/Z_2)
 148     model1 : str
 149         Name of first model (positive BF favors this)
 150     model2 : str
 151         Name of second model (negative BF favors this)
 152     """
 153     abs_bf = abs(ln_bf)
 154     if abs_bf < 1:
 155         strength = "Inconclusive"
 156     elif abs_bf < 2.5:
 157         strength = "Weak"
 158     elif abs_bf < 5:
 159         strength = "Moderate"
 160     else:
 161         strength = "Strong"
 162 
 163     direction = f"favors {model1}" if ln_bf > 0 else f"favors {model2}"
 164     return f"{strength} evidence {direction} (ln(BF) = {ln_bf:.2f})"
 165

 167 class _PriorTransform:
 168     """Picklable prior transform (unit cube -> parameter space) for dynesty.
 169 
 170     A module-level callable instance, not a closure, so it can be pickled to
 171     multiprocessing/dynesty.pool workers.
 172     """
 173 
 174     def __init__(
 175         self,
 176         priors: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]],
 177         param_names: Tuple[str, ...],
 178         log_params: Tuple[str, ...] = ("c0", "tau_1ghz", "zeta"),
 179     ):
 180         self.priors = priors
 181         self.param_names = param_names
 182         self.log_params = log_params
 183 
 184     def __call__(self, u: NDArray[np.floating]) -> NDArray[np.floating]:
 185         theta = np.zeros_like(u)
 186         for i, name in enumerate(self.param_names):
 187             lo, hi = self.priors[name]
 188             if name in self.log_params and lo > 0 and hi > 0:
 189                 log_lo, log_hi = np.log(lo), np.log(hi)
 190                 theta[i] = np.exp(log_lo + u[i] * (log_hi - log_lo))
 191             else:
 192                 theta[i] = lo + u[i] * (hi - lo)
 193         return theta
 194 
 195 
 196 def _build_prior_transform(
 197     priors: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]],
 198     param_names: Tuple[str, ...],
 199     log_params: Tuple[str, ...] = ("c0", "tau_1ghz", "zeta"),
 200 ):
 201     """Return a picklable prior-transform callable for dynesty."""
 202     return _PriorTransform(priors, param_names, log_params)
 203 
 204 
 205 class _LogLikelihood:
 206     """Picklable log-likelihood callable for dynesty.
 207 
 208     Module-level callable (not a closure) so dynesty.pool can ship it to
 209     worker processes; FRBModel holds only numpy arrays + scalars and pickles.
 210     Optional Gaussian priors on alpha / log10(tau) are folded into the
 211     log-likelihood (dynesty's prior_transform handles the rest).
 212     """
 213 
 214     def __init__(
 215         self,
 216         model: FRBModel,
 217         model_key: str,
 218         param_names: Tuple[str, ...],
 219         beta_prior: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
 220         alpha_prior: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
 221         tau_prior: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
 222         likelihood_kind: str = "gaussian",
 223         student_nu: float = 5.0,
 224         fixed_params: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
 225     ):
 226         self.model = model
 227         self.model_key = model_key
 228         self.param_names = param_names
 229         self.full_param_names = _PARAM_KEYS[model_key]
 230         self.beta_prior = beta_prior
 231         if self.beta_prior is None and alpha_prior is not None:
 232             mu_a, sigma_a = alpha_prior
 233             if sigma_a is None or sigma_a <= 0.0:
 234                 # (mu, None) encodes "fixed alpha"; fixing is handled by
 235                 # fixed_params / the prior transform, not a Gaussian factor.
 236                 self.beta_prior = None
 237             else:
 238                 # Jacobian-convert the width: sigma_beta = sigma_alpha *
 239                 # 4/(alpha-2)^2 (same transform as apply_physical_priors).
 240                 self.beta_prior = (
 241                     beta_from_alpha_thin_screen(mu_a),
 242                     sigma_a * 4.0 / (mu_a - 2.0) ** 2,
 243                 )
 244         self.tau_prior = tau_prior
 245         self.likelihood_kind = likelihood_kind
 246         self.student_nu = student_nu
 247         self.fixed_params = fixed_params
 248 
 249     def __call__(self, theta: NDArray[np.floating]) -> float:
 250         if self.fixed_params:
 251             full_theta = []
 252             theta_ptr = 0
 253             for name in self.full_param_names:
 254                 if name in self.fixed_params:
 255                     full_theta.append(self.fixed_params[name])
 256                 else:
 257                     full_theta.append(theta[theta_ptr])
 258                     theta_ptr += 1
 259             params = FRBParams.from_sequence(full_theta, self.model_key)
 260         else:
 261             params = FRBParams.from_sequence(theta, self.model_key)
 262 
 263         if self.likelihood_kind == "gaussian":
 264             ll = self.model.log_likelihood(params, self.model_key)
 265         else:
 266             ll = self.model.log_likelihood_student_t(
 267                 params, self.model_key, nu=self.student_nu
 268             )
 269 
 270         if not np.isfinite(ll):
 271             return -1e100
 272 
 273         if self.beta_prior is not None and "beta" in self.param_names:
 274             mu, sigma = self.beta_prior
 275             ll += -0.5 * ((params.beta - mu) / sigma) ** 2
 276 
 277         if self.tau_prior is not None and "tau_1ghz" in self.param_names:
 278             mu_log10, sigma_log10 = self.tau_prior
 279             tau = params.tau_1ghz
 280             if tau > 0:
 281                 ll += -0.5 * ((np.log10(tau) - mu_log10) / sigma_log10) ** 2
 282             else:
 283                 ll = -1e100
 284 
 285         return ll
 286 
 287 
 288 def _build_log_likelihood(
 289     model: FRBModel,
 290     model_key: str,
 291     param_names: Tuple[str, ...],
 292     beta_prior: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
 293     alpha_prior: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
 294     tau_prior: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
 295     likelihood_kind: str = "gaussian",
 296     student_nu: float = 5.0,
 297     fixed_params: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
 298 ):
 299     """Return a picklable log-likelihood callable for dynesty."""
 300     return _LogLikelihood(
 301         model, model_key, param_names, beta_prior, alpha_prior, tau_prior,
 302         likelihood_kind, student_nu, fixed_params,
 303     )
